info.title: Propel Site BOM API
info.summary: Create, read, edit, baseline and reconcile a Site BOM.
info.description:
The complete REST surface of Propel's Site BOM, built on Propel's
**branch / baseline / configuration-item** framework. It covers the whole lifecycle: create a Site BOM over a released eBOM revision, read its structure, edit it with
delta operations, freeze it as a baseline, and reconcile it against a newer eBOM revision.

---

## Read this first: the eight ideas the whole API rests on

### 1. A Site BOM inherits its structure. It never copies it.

Creating a Site BOM writes **four records and not one row of BOM structure**. The branch stores
only its own *deltas*; everything else is resolved at read time by walking the eBOM's live
`Assembly__c` lines beneath the accepted eBOM root revision. An untouched branch holds zero
per-edge records however many times it is read.

### 2. `T_R` — the pinned source clock

When a Site BOM is created (or a pull is committed), the accepted root revision's
**release date** is stamped once on the Site BOM's source and reported as `sourceTimePoint`. That
timestamp is **T_R**, and every
`base` row resolves against it: a child item renders at whichever revision was released as
of T_R.

T_R is *stamped, then read* — never re-derived. So when engineering releases `Assy-100` rev-2,
**nothing happens to the Site BOM**. It still resolves against rev-1's T_R until someone explicitly
accepts the newer revision with a [pull](#tag/Pull).

### 3. `asOf` — the branch clock, and why there are two

Every read also takes an `asOf` timestamp (defaulting to now). That one governs the *branch's*
own content — its deltas, its locally added parts, its substitutes.

Two clocks are therefore legitimately in play at once, and each row states which one governs it
(`TreeRow.governingTimestamp`, `MemberState.governingClock`):

| Row kind | Governing clock |
|---|---|
| `base` — supplied by the source, untouched | **T_R** (`source`) |
| `claiming` — the branch took copy-on-write ownership of a source row | **`asOf`** (`branch`) for its quantity and find number |
| `new` — branch-owned, no upstream provenance | **`asOf`** (`branch`) |
| a *substitute* (from `replace`) | **`asOf`** — its child floats |

A direct consequence is that **one item can render at two different revisions in the same
tree**. That is expected, not a fault, and is reported as a `MIXED_REVISION` finding (see
[findings](#operation/getBranchFindings)) rather than as an error.

#### A third answer: a chosen revision

A row's **child revision** can also be the caller's explicit choice rather than any clock's
output. Every operation that creates or takes over a row (`claim`, `add`, `replace`,
`convert-to-native`) accepts a `childItemRevisionId`; a row that stores one is **pinned** and
renders exactly that revision whatever T_R or `asOf` say, and reports
`TreeRow.hasChosenRevision: true`. An `update` changes or clears the stored revision
afterwards. A row that stores none **tracks**:

| Row | Stored revision | Child revision it renders |
|---|---|---|
| tracking claim (`trackChildRevision: true`) | none | the source line's own, at **T_R** — it moves when a pull accepts a newer source |
| `new` row / substitute, no revision sent | none | whatever is released at **`asOf`** (floats) |
| tracking convert (`trackChildRevision: true`) | none | floats at **`asOf`**, like an `add` — it has no source left to follow |
| any pinned row | `childItemRevisionId` | the pin, always |

`claim` and `convert-to-native` have no default and must say which they want — see the
[delta endpoint](#operation/applyDeltaBatch). A row pinned to a revision **other than** the one
its source line resolves to renders that revision's own structure beneath it, read-only, in
place of the source's lines.

### 4. Provenance: `base` / `claiming` / `new`

Derived at read time, never stored. `claiming` and `new` differ only in whether the branch's
row took over a source line (`claiming`) or has no upstream line at all (`new`), and that
difference is what makes "what did I change relative to upstream?" answerable. A fourth
value, `nested`, marks the read-only rows beneath a locally added or substituted assembly, or
beneath a pinned row.

### 5. Copy-on-write: you must `claim` before you can edit

A `base` row is read-only. Editing it is refused with `CLAIM_REQUIRED`, carrying the eBOM
line id so the client can offer the claim. Divergence from upstream is always an explicit act.
`update` with `autoClaim: true` claims and revises in one operation. It is still
explicit, and the result reports `claimed: true`.

### 6. Nothing is ever deleted

Removal is an **exclude delta** — a tombstone appended to an append-only log. `restore` lifts
it. A hard delete of any branch-owned row is refused (`HARD_DELETE_BLOCKED`). This is what makes
a read at a past `asOf`, and therefore a baseline, reproducible.

### 7. A baseline stores a timepoint, not rows

Cutting a baseline records one timestamp and freezes the revisions it resolved to. Reading it
**re-resolves** the branch at that timestamp. Three stored counts act as canaries if something
the resolution depends on has moved since — `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` for the row count,
`BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` for how many of those rows are the branch's own claims, and
`BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT` for how many hold an explicitly chosen revision. They are reported by the
baseline's
[findings](#operation/getBaselineFindings).

### 8. "Pull", not "merge"

A pull is the **downstream-initiated acceptance of a newer upstream source version**. The word
*merge* is deliberately reserved for a branch-to-branch operation in a later version, which is
bidirectional and common-ancestor-based — genuinely different.

---

## Response and error conventions

These conventions differ from other Propel REST endpoints:

- Success and error bodies are **plain JSON, never wrapped** in an
  `entity` / `entities` envelope.
- **Error bodies key the code as `code`, not `errorCode`.** `errorCode` appears in this API only
  *inside* a delta batch's per-operation `results[]`.
- **Nulls are not suppressed.** A field left null for that case is meaningfully null — see
  `DeltaResult.forked`, where `null` and `false` say different things.
- **The code is the contract; the message is not.** Messages are translated. Switch on `code`,
  never on text.

### Status-code scheme

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **202** | *Reserved.* A whole-configuration output, a pull preview or a pull commit accepted as a background job (`status: accepted`, `jobId`). Never answered in this version; handle it now so a later version breaks nothing. |
| **400** | The request could not be read, or a value is out of range. Fix the request. |
| **403** | No permission. The body carries the label only — never the object that was denied. |
| **404** | The path, an id in the body, or a `parentRowKey` names nothing. |
| **409** | Well formed, and **retryable after changing state** — claim it first, restore it first, reload, re-preview. |
| **413** | Too large for one transaction. `BATCH_TOO_LARGE`: more than 200 operations in one delta batch — split the request. `STRUCTURE_TOO_LARGE`: the structure the request has to resolve exceeds what one transaction can process — no retry of the same request will succeed. |
| **422** | Well formed, but **impossible against the model**. Retrying unchanged will never succeed (a cycle is still a cycle). |
| **500** | Unmodelled server failure. Carries the error type only — never its message or the stack trace. |

The 409/422 split is deliberate: a client that retries on a generic 4xx would spin forever on a
cycle, and the two cases want different UI.

---

## Paging, row identity and snapshots

No read in this API returns a whole configuration in one response. Every structure read and
every change list is paged, and a client must not assume that one response is the whole tree.

- **Pages.** A paged response carries `page: {limit, hasMore, nextCursor}`. Send `nextCursor`
  back as `cursor` to get the next page. A cursor continues the request that issued it: the
  query is read from the cursor, so every other parameter except `limit` is ignored beside it.
  Cursors are opaque, do not expire, and must not be parsed. **There is no total row count.**
  `hasMore` is the only end-of-data signal.
- **Rows.** Every tree row carries a server-issued `rowKey`, its parent's `parentRowKey`, a
  `level` (1 for the root's children) and `hasChildren`. Two occurrences of one item get two
  different `rowKey`s, so a client re-nests rows by `parentRowKey`, never by item id. Children
  are fetched by `rowKey`; the client never composes a resolution input.
- **`rowKey`** encodes the row's occurrence path from the root. It is URL-safe, at most 16
  characters per level, and **stable** while that occurrence exists: across edits, across
  snapshots, and across sessions. It changes only when the occurrence itself changes, for
  example when a pull moves a parent to a revision whose BOM lines are new records.
- **`snapshot`.** Every structure read returns an opaque `snapshot` naming the state it
  resolved. Send it back on child and page requests and they resolve the same rows, even if
  the branch is edited in between. It pins **which rows exist and where**. A Draft row's
  quantity or find number edited in place after the snapshot shows its newer value. Edits
  do not check what the caller last read: the last write wins (see the
  [delta endpoint](#operation/applyDeltaBatch)).
- **Whole-configuration outputs are their own resources.** The flattened view and the
  findings (whole-configuration warnings) are separate endpoints, not modes of the tree read.
  Each answers `200` today, and may answer `202 Accepted` + `jobId` for a large configuration
  in a later version.

---

## Design intent: Site BOM-specific paths, generic vocabulary

Site BOM is the first application of a general branch / baseline / configuration-item framework. The
path is namespaced under `/site-bom` so Site BOM-only rules have somewhere to live, but the nouns below
that segment — **branch**, **source**, **member**, **claim**, **baseline** — are framework
concepts, not Site BOM concepts. Everything Site BOM-specific is confined to a single discriminated
schema, `AssemblyEdgeDetail`, reached through `MemberState.detail` and keyed by `ciKind`. A
second configuration-item type adds a sibling schema there and touches nothing else.

## Paths

There is **no `branchId` path segment on the source endpoints**: a source already names its
owning branch. `branchId` still appears in the pull-preview *body*, denormalised for display.

post.summary: Create a Site BOM over a released eBOM revision
post.description:
Creates a Site BOM header, its first branch, the branch's eBOM source lineage, and that
source's first acceptance — **four records in one transaction, and zero rows of BOM
structure**.

The response returns all four ids rather than just `siteBomId`, because a caller that had to go
looking for the other three would be querying schema this API exists to hide. The one you
will use most is `sourceId` — it is the `sourceId` every `/sources/...` endpoint
takes.

## The root revision must be Released

Its `Released_Date_Time__c` becomes **T_R**, the timepoint every `base` row resolves at.
An unreleased revision has no such date, so there is nothing to pin to.

Four shapes are refused with `NOT_RELEASED` (409, not 400 — releasing the revision makes the
identical request succeed): not released; **Cancelled**; **Expired**; released but carrying
no release date. Cancelled and Expired are excluded because the eBOM's own as-of read would
never resolve them either.

## Timestamps stamped here

| Field | Value | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **T_R** (reported as `sourceTimePoint`) | the root revision's release date | what `base` rows resolve at, forever |
| the acceptance time | the **wall clock**, now | which acceptance governs a given `asOf` |

A consequence worth knowing before you write a test: because the acceptance time is the wall
clock, a branch created now renders **nothing** when read at an `asOf` in the past. That is
the acceptance not existing yet at that timestamp, not a defect.

## Access

Gated **before the body is read**: a caller with no create grant gets 403 whatever they sent.
Requires create on `Site_BOM__c`, `Branch__c`, `Branch_Source__c` and
`Branch_Source_Rev__c`, plus read on `Item_Revision__c`. All five are checked up front, so a
partial grant is a clean 403 rather than a 500 partway through the create.

standard.summary: A Site BOM over Assy-100 rev-1

201.description:
Created. Four records now exist. 201 rather than 200 because the response names records
that did not exist before the call, and a client distinguishing "created" from "already
there" has nothing else to read.

400.description:
`INVALID_REQUEST` — the body was empty or unreadable; `siteBomName` or `branchLabel` was
blank; or either exceeded its field length (`siteBomName` ≤ 80, `branchLabel` ≤ 80).

A malformed id in the **body** is a 400 while one in the **URI** is a 404, and that is
not an inconsistency: the URI is what *names* the resource, so a path naming nothing is
a path to nothing. A body field is a value in a request to a resource that does exist.

value.message: That request could not be read. Check that the body is valid JSON and that every required value is supplied. (siteBomName is required)

404.description:
`NOT_FOUND` — `rootItemRevisionId` was null, is not an `Item_Revision__c` id, or names
no visible row. The three are not distinguished on purpose: separating "malformed" from
"absent" would tell an unauthorised caller which ids exist.

value.message: That record does not exist, or you do not have access to it. (a0Bg8000000Ab10EAC is not an Item_Revision__c)

409.description:
`NOT_RELEASED` — the root revision is unreleased, Cancelled, Expired, or has no release
date, so there is no T_R to stamp.

value.message: A Site BOM can only be created from a released item revision. (a0Ag8000000Ab99EAC)

get.description:
The branch's resolved content at one timepoint: the eBOM traversed at **T_R**, with the
branch's own deltas folded and overlaid at **`asOf`**.

This is the main read. It is where the two-clock model becomes visible — every row states
its own `provenance` and its own `governingTimestamp`, because a row that did not carry its
own clock would be unexplainable to the person looking at it.

## What the response contains that you might not expect

- **Excluded rows are rendered**, carrying `isExcluded: true`. A tree read shows the person
  editing what was removed. (A *baseline* read filters them out — see that endpoint.)
- **`isEditable: false`** on any row inside the subtree of a locally added or substituted
  assembly, or of a row holding a chosen revision **other than** its source line's (below).
  Only content the branch's *source* supplied can be
  claimed or changed. It is stated rather than left to be derived from `provenance`, so a
  client does not have to encode which provenance values happen to be editable this
  release. Every delta op refuses these rows (`NOT_EDITABLE`), so a UI offering an action on
  one is offering an action the API will reject.
- **A row holding a different revision renders that revision's structure.** A row whose chosen
  `childItemRevisionId` differs from the revision its source line resolves to at T_R gets
  that revision's eBOM beneath it as read-only `nested` rows, and the source's lines under
  it are suppressed. A branch edit sitting on one of those suppressed lines — a claim,
  exclusion, update or substitute, or an `add` under an item only the suppressed structure
  supplied — takes no effect, and the read says so with `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` on
  the pinned row rather than failing.
- **Each occurrence renders its own structure.** One item can render in two
  places at two revisions — one occurrence pinned and another still at the source's
  revision, or two pins. Each occurrence follows its own revision: a pinned occurrence
  renders that revision's `nested` rows beneath it, and an unpinned occurrence keeps the
  source's lines. An edit on a suppressed line is hidden only when no occurrence still
  renders that line, and `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` is then raised once per pinned row
  and hidden item, each warning carrying the pinned row's `rowKey` and the hidden item.
  `MIXED_REVISION` is still reported, on the
  [findings](#operation/getBranchFindings), never blocking. A branch `add` under such an
  item binds to the item, not to one rendering: it appears under **every** occurrence,
  with no warning of its own, and survives the parent advancing to a newer revision. Where
  an occurrence's own structure has a line at the same position as the `add` (same parent
  item, child item and discriminator), only the `add` renders there, so the occurrence
  never shows two identical rows. Each
  occurrence, and each of its children, has its own `rowKey`, so a client places every row
  under the right occurrence by `parentRowKey`.
- **A row whose source line is gone renders only where the source's structure does
 .** A claim or exclusion on a line upstream has since removed (see
  `claim-orphaned` on the pull) still hangs under its parent item, but only beneath an
  occurrence showing the source's own structure of that item. Beneath a pinned row, or
  inside a locally added or substituted assembly's `nested` copy of the item at another
  revision, a different structure renders, so the row does not appear there. A copy at
  the very revision the source renders is the same structure and shows it too.
- **An edit on a revision nothing renders does not appear.** A claim sits on its line's
  parent revision. If no occurrence renders that revision any more, for example because
  the branch excluded the parent's own line and added the parent item back, floating to a
  later revision, the claim renders nowhere. No warning is raised, because no pin hid it.
  It is still the branch's: it is addressable as below, and a pull whose candidate drops
  its line still reports it as `claim-orphaned`.
- **A substitute never absorbs another line of its new child.** When a
  `replace` substitute's child item also has its own, unrelated eBOM line under the same
  parent, both render. The substitute is its own row with its own
  `replaces-{branchId}-{supersededEdgeKey}-{newChildItemId}` key, and the other line keeps
  its own row and `edgeKey`. The ambiguous position match is declined rather than refused,
  so this read never answers `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION`. If upstream later makes the same
  substitution itself, two rows render — the substitute beside upstream's new line —
  rather than one.
- **Every row says whether its revision was a choice.** `hasChosenRevision` is
  true exactly when the row stores a chosen child revision — even one equal to what the
  clock would pick. A clock-resolved row, a row beneath a pin (`nested`) and a floating
  `new` row are `false`. Where it is true, `revisionChosenById` / `revisionChosenAt` name
  the creator and creation time of the branch revision the row resolves through.
  `wasClaimed` marks a `new` row that `convert-to-native` flipped from `claiming`. All of
  them follow the explicit decision, not the structural pin above.
- **A dead stored revision is warned about, never replaced.** A row whose stored
  `childItemRevisionId` has since been Cancelled or Expired still renders that revision,
  and the read raises one `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` per such row. The comparison raises it
  too, on both a branch and a baseline side; the baseline tree read and the pull preview
  do not.
- **Unreachable rows are dropped.** A delta can name a parent item that is not in the tree —
  a subassembly whose item had nothing released at T_R drops out, and a claim beneath it
  survives the overlay as a row with an absent parent. This read walks down from the root and
  keeps only what it can reach.
- **`warnings` and `rows` are always present**, empty rather than absent. A client that has
  to distinguish "no warnings" from "the key is missing" writes null checks at every call
  site, and one of them is eventually forgotten.

## Paging and expanding

Rows come in **depth-first pre-order**: every row is followed by its own descendants before
its next sibling. Siblings with no find number come first; the rest are ordered by find
number, then child item number, then a stable server-defined tie-break.

| Request | Returns |
|---|---|
| no `parentRowKey`, `depth` omitted | the whole tree, paged by `limit` (default 500) |
| no `parentRowKey`, `depth=1` | the root's children only — the first level of a grid |
| `parentRowKey=<rowKey>`, `depth=1` | that row's children — expanding one row in a grid |
| `parentRowKey=<rowKey>`, `depth` omitted | that row's whole subtree, not the row itself |

`hasChildren` says whether a children request for the row would return anything. A shared
subassembly appears under every occurrence that renders it, each copy with its own
`rowKey`, because that is what a BOM tree looks like to a person expanding it.

Send the response's `snapshot` with every child and page request belonging to one view, so
they all resolve the same rows. Without it, a child request resolves the branch as it is
now, at `asOf`. A `rowKey` stays valid across snapshots while its occurrence exists; one
that no longer names a row answers `404 NOT_FOUND`.

## Warnings on this read

`warnings` lists only warnings about **rows in this response**, each naming its row by
`rowKey`, and each row lists its own codes in `warningCodes`:

| Code | Raised on |
|---|---|
| `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` | the row whose stored revision was Cancelled or Expired |
| `MEMBER_ADD_COLLISION` | the collapsed row (`isCollapsedCollision: true`) |
| `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` | the pinned row whose structure hides the edits — one per pinned row and hidden item |
| `NESTED_CYCLE_PRUNED` | the row whose nested structure was dropped |
| `REDLINE_AMBIGUOUS` | with `compare=`, each row the redline could not pair |

Warnings about the configuration as a whole — `MIXED_REVISION` — are not computed by a page
and are not on this read. The [findings](#operation/getBranchFindings) report them, with every
row-level warning beside them.

## Redlines: `compare=`

`compare` adds a **redline** to every row: how this tree differs from a second
configuration. Rows are paired with the same correlation join the
[comparison](#operation/compareBranch) uses, so a redline and the comparison's entry for the
same position always agree, and `redline.entryId` is that entry's `entryId`.

| `compare` | Compares against |
|---|---|
| `source` | what this branch's own source supplies — "what has this Site BOM changed?" |
| `baseline:{baselineId}` | a baseline, at its own recorded timepoint |
| `branch:{branchId}` | another branch, now |
| `ebom:{itemRevisionId}` | a released eBOM revision, at its release date |

`redline.status` reads **this tree against the target**:

| status | Meaning | Matching comparison kind |
|---|---|---|
| `added` | this tree has the row; the target does not | `member-removed` |
| `removed` | the target has the row; this tree does not | `member-added` |
| `modified` | both have it; `changedFields` lists what differs and `oldValues` holds the target's values | `member-differs` |
| `unchanged` | both have it, identical | `member-unchanged` |

Note that the comparison names its kinds from the **target's** point of view, so `added`
here matches `member-removed` there.

- **A removed row is rendered** under every occurrence of its parent item in this tree,
  with the target's own subtree beneath it, all `removed`. Its `detail` is the target's. It
  is not a row of this branch: `edgeId` and `ciId` are null, and `isEditable` is
  false. A row beneath a removed row carries the comparison's `entryId` for its position
  when the comparison reports that position as `member-added`, and a null `entryId` when
  the comparison pairs that position elsewhere in this tree.
- **An excluded row is `removed` itself**, not duplicated: the branch renders its tombstone,
  and the target still has the line.
- **`hasChildren`** is true when either side has children, so a row whose children were
  all removed still expands.
- **A position the join cannot pair degrades.** Rather than answering
  `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` as the comparison does, the read renders the rows unpaired, as
  `added` and `removed`, each carrying `REDLINE_AMBIGUOUS`. A grid should not blank out
  over one odd line.
- **`snapshot` pins both sides**, so a child page joins against the same target state.
- The target is described once, on the response, as `compareTarget`.

## Reads create nothing

Nothing is written on this path. An untouched branch stays at zero rows however many times
it is read.

200.description: One page of the resolved tree.

wholeTree.summary: The whole tree in one page — base, claiming, new and excluded rows

firstLevelPaged.summary: `depth=1&limit=2` — the first level of a grid, with more to come

pinnedClaim.summary: A claim pinned to another revision — its structure nested beneath, and a hidden edit warned

400.description:
`ASOF_INVALID` — `asOf` could not be parsed. `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` — `asOf` is later than now;
there is no configuration at a timepoint that has not happened.

`INVALID_REQUEST` — `limit` or `depth` is not a positive integer (or `all` for
`depth`); `cursor` or `snapshot` is not one this endpoint issued for this branch; or
`compare` is not one of the four forms.

value.message: The timepoint could not be read. Use an ISO-8601 timestamp, for example 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z. (yesterday)
That request could not be read. Check that the body is valid JSON and that every required value is supplied. (cursor was not issued by this endpoint for this branch)

404.description:
`NOT_FOUND` — the path id names no branch (see `NotFoundPath`); `parentRowKey` names no
row in the state being read; or a `compare` target names nothing, or the wrong object.

value.message: That record does not exist, or you do not have access to it. (parentRowKey a0Bg8000000Ab77 names no row in this tree)

409.description: `NOT_RELEASED` — `compare=ebom:{id}` names a revision that is not Released, or is Cancelled, Expired, or has no release date.

422.description:
`EBOM_CYCLE` — the source eBOM itself contains a cycle, so its structure cannot be
resolved. Fix the eBOM; retrying is pointless. With `compare`, a cycle beneath the
target's root is `CYCLE_DETECTED`, as on the comparison. A redline never answers
`AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION`; it degrades instead (see above).

get.summary: Read what a source supplies, with no branch deltas applied
get.description:
The "**what would I inherit?**" read: the structure as one source supplies it, with the
branch's claims, excludes and replaces deliberately **not** overlaid.

Use it to answer "what did I change relative to upstream?" by diffing this against
`GET /site-bom/branches/{branchId}/tree`, or read the branch with `compare=source`. Every row
comes back `provenance: base`.

Paging, `rowKey`s and `snapshot` work exactly as on the
[branch tree read](#operation/getBranchTree). There is no `compare` here. A source
stores no revisions, so its rows raise no row warnings except `NESTED_CYCLE_PRUNED`.

200.description: One page of the source's own structure.

400.description: `ASOF_INVALID`, `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` or `INVALID_REQUEST` — see the branch tree read.

404.description: `NOT_FOUND` — the path id names no source, or `parentRowKey` names no row.

422.description: `EBOM_CYCLE` — the source eBOM contains a cycle.

get.summary: Read a branch's flattened structure — one line per part, quantities summed
get.description:
The branch's structure collapsed to **one line per part**: every occurrence of a part
anywhere in the tree, with its quantity multiplied down the path from the root and summed.
This is what a planner or a costing integration needs ("how many of each part does one
build take?") and what the eBOM grid's flattened view shows.

## What is one line

A line is one **child item + rendered revision + secondary unique key**:

- **Quantities multiply, then sum.** A part used 2 per subassembly, in a subassembly used 3
  per root, counts 6. The same part elsewhere in the tree adds to that line.
- **One item at two revisions is two lines**, each carrying `MIXED_REVISION` in
  `warningCodes`. The quantities are never merged across revisions.
- **Only what the configuration contains** is counted. An excluded row, and everything its
  exclusion prunes, adds nothing. Read-only `nested` rows count: they are real structure.
- The root item is not a line; it is the thing being built.

For a Site BOM with no branch edits, the lines equal the eBOM grid's flattened view of the same
root revision at the same time.

## A whole-configuration output

Every line depends on every occurrence in the tree, so even the first page needs the whole
structure. That is why this is its own resource rather than a mode of the tree read. It
answers `200` today. A later version may answer a very large configuration
`202 Accepted` with `status: accepted` and a `jobId`. Handle `status` now.

Lines are ordered by child item number, then revision label, then secondary unique key,
and paged by `limit` (default 500) and `cursor`. Each page continues after the last line
the previous page returned, and the set of lines is fixed by the state the first page
resolved. A Draft row's quantity edited in place between pages shows in the totals of
later pages.

## Access

Read access, as the branch tree read. Nothing is written.

post.summary: Apply a batch of delta operations to a branch
post.description:
The single write endpoint for editing a branch. Eight operations — `claim`, `update`, `add`,
`exclude`, `restore`, `replace`, `revert`, `convert-to-native` — arrive in one array and are
applied under one envelope. There is no `set-revision` operation: `update` is the one row
edit, and changes or clears a stored child revision too. `"op": "set-revision"`
answers `INVALID_REQUEST` (`unknown op set-revision`), like any unknown op.

**Returns `200`, not `201`**, even though rows are created: the response is a *report* on a
set of operations, not a pointer to one new resource, and under `atomic: false` some of them
may have failed.

## How a batch executes

1. **Size check** — more than 200 operations is `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` (413), refused before
   anything is resolved.
2. **One snapshot.** The branch is resolved **once**, at `asOf`. That is the whole reason a
   batch endpoint exists: twenty operations resolving the branch each would be twenty
   traversals, and the tree could shift underneath the batch halfway through.
3. **Validate everything, then apply.** Two passes, never interleaved, so *every* fault is
   reported rather than only the first.
4. **Persist** in a fixed number of database writes — twenty claims cost the same writes as
   one.

### Order is preserved, but order is not sequencing

Results come back in request order with your `clientRef` echoed and `index` stated. But
**every operation validates against the one pre-batch snapshot, so a later operation cannot
see an earlier one's effect.** `[claim(L), update(L)]` in one batch answers `CLAIM_REQUIRED`
on the update — and under the default `atomic: true` that rejects the whole batch.

> **Dependent edits are two requests, not two operations.**

> The most common dependent pair, claim then change a quantity, is **one** operation:
> `{"op": "update", "ebomAssemblyId": "…", "quantity": 3, "autoClaim": true, "trackChildRevision": true}`.
> The batch still does not sequence, so `[claim(L), update(L)]` still answers
> `CLAIM_REQUIRED`. Send that payload only to a row you know is `base`: on a row the branch
> already owns, `trackChildRevision: true` **clears** whatever revision the row stores
> (see below).

### Two operations on one row in one batch

Operations that fork or edit a row's current revision are mutually exclusive in one batch;
a content edit followed by an operation that only appends a later delta is a coherent
sequence, and both apply. The second of a refused pair answers `INVALID_REQUEST`.

- Every `update` that writes takes the row's **revise slot**: a second `update` of the row
  is refused (`already revised earlier in this same batch`). So is a `convert-to-native`
  that stamps a revision different from the stored one (it forks), beside an `update`, in
  either order.
- An `update` that **changes the stored revision**, or that claims (`autoClaim`), also takes
  the row's **membership slot**: beside a `claim`, `revert`, `exclude`, `restore`,
  `replace`, any `convert-to-native` or another such `update` of the same row, the second
  is refused (`that row already has a membership change earlier in this same batch`).
- Still allowed: a quantity / find-number-only `update` beside `revert`, `exclude`, or a
  `convert-to-native` that keeps the stored revision.
- A revision-only `update` the row already satisfies writes nothing and takes no slot.

## `atomic` — the failure contract is yours to choose

| `atomic` | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `true` (**default** — a null wins the safer contract) | All-or-nothing. Any validation failure throws: the status is the **first failure's** own code (so a batch whose only fault is `CLAIM_REQUIRED` still answers 409, not a generic 400) and the body carries a `failures[]` array with **every** failure. The branch is left exactly as it was. |
| `false` | Apply what is valid, report the rest. `200` with per-operation `results[]`. |

`atomic: false` reports per-operation **validation** failures only. It does not fall back to
saving operation by operation: the valid operations are saved together, and a failure while
saving rolls the whole batch back and is returned as an error.

## `asOf` chooses what a batch *validates* against; it never dates the write

Every row written is effective **now**, whatever `asOf` says. A past `asOf` means "validate
against the configuration as it stood then" — optimistic concurrency, not time travel.
Backdating the write would let a batch win the current state *and* change what a read at an
intervening timestamp returned, rewriting history in an append-only log.

Several operations therefore **refuse a past `asOf` outright** with `INVALID_REQUEST`,
because they decide from the branch's *current* state: `restore`, `revert`,
`convert-to-native`, and any `claim` / `add` / `exclude` / `replace` that has to mint a new
edge identity.

## Last write wins

An operation does not check whether someone else changed its row since the caller read
it. An edit of a row another user changed in the meantime applies over their change, and
the last write wins. There is no row-level or branch-wide precondition to send. Site BOM
editing is not a high-concurrency workload, so this keeps the contract simple.

Every write but one keeps the state it replaced in the branch's history. `claim`,
`exclude`, `restore`, `revert`, `convert-to-native` and `replace` append to the branch's
delta log, and an `update` that forks creates a new revision beside the old one. The
exception is an `update` that edits a Draft revision in place (`forked: false`): it
rewrites that revision and keeps no copy of the value it replaced.

## After the write: `snapshot` and `invalidatedParentRowKeys`

A successful response carries the `snapshot` of the branch **after** the write, and
`invalidatedParentRowKeys`: the rows whose children a client should fetch again, because a
row beneath them was added, removed or changed. An empty string in the list stands for the
root. Re-reading those rows' children with the new `snapshot` brings a grid up to date
without reloading the whole tree.

## `Idempotency-Key`

Read and passed through, and **ignored in this version**. It is accepted so a client can start
sending it now without its first request failing, and a later version can honour it without a
breaking change.

## The operations

| `op` | Required fields | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `claim` | `ebomAssemblyId`, and **exactly one of** `childItemRevisionId` \| `trackChildRevision: true` | Takes one live eBOM line into the branch as a copy-on-write claim, so the branch can diverge from it. Copies quantity and find number as they stand; the child revision is the caller's choice — a chosen revision **pins** it, `trackChildRevision: true` **tracks** the source line at T_R. Writes 5 records. |
| `update` | `assemblyCiId` **or** `ebomAssemblyId`; **at least one of** `quantity`, `findNumber`, `childItemRevisionId`, `trackChildRevision: true`; optional `autoClaim` | Revises a branch-owned edge. Omitted fields keep the row's value. Without a revision change it edits the row's current revision in place while that is Draft (`forked: false`), otherwise allocates a new revision, freezes the old one, and returns `forked: true`. A `childItemRevisionId` different from the one the row **stores** pins it to that revision; `trackChildRevision: true` clears a stored revision. A revision change **always forks** (`forked: true`, even over a Draft). With `autoClaim: true` it also claims a `base` edge first (see `DeltaOperation.autoClaim`). |
| `add` | `parentItemId`, `childItemId`, `quantity`, `findNumber`; optional `childItemRevisionId` | Adds a part the eBOM never supplied — packaging, fixtures, consumables. Provenance `new`. The child **floats** at `asOf`, unless `childItemRevisionId` pins it. |
| `exclude` | `ebomAssemblyId` **or** `ciId` | Tombstones a row. **No cascade is written** — the descendant prune is computed at read time, because a descendant still supplied through another path must survive. |
| `restore` | `ciId` | Lifts an exclusion. A row the branch holds its own content for renders that content again; a `base` row that was excluded without being claimed falls back to what its source supplies. |
| `replace` | `replacedEbomAssemblyId`, `newChildItemId`, `quantity`, `findNumber`; optional `childItemRevisionId` | Substitutes a different child for the one an eBOM line supplies, **recording that it is a substitution**, so the pair does not read as an unrelated removal plus an unrelated addition. The substitute floats at `asOf` unless `childItemRevisionId` pins it. |
| `revert` | `ciId` **or** `ebomAssemblyId` | Discards the branch's claim so the row falls back to what its source supplies. Nothing is deleted: the revert is recorded in the branch log, and the branch content for the row stops applying. |
| `convert-to-native` | `ciId`, and **exactly one of** `childItemRevisionId` \| `trackChildRevision: true` | Severs a claiming edge's link to the source it claims: same quantity and find number, but now branch-owned in its own right (`provenance` flips `claiming` → `new`). The child revision is the caller's choice — a chosen revision is stamped on, `trackChildRevision: true` floats at `asOf`. |

### `update` in detail

One `update` saves everything a line editor holds — quantity, find number and revision —
in one operation and, when the revision changes, one fork. A pull's `accept-fields`
decision compiles to exactly one `update` too.

- **Omitted = keep**, for every field. A null `childItemRevisionId` alone is not a clear;
  clearing is spelled `trackChildRevision: true`. Sending none of `quantity`, `findNumber`,
  `childItemRevisionId`, `trackChildRevision: true` answers `INVALID_REQUEST`
  (`update requires quantity, findNumber, childItemRevisionId or trackChildRevision: true`).
- **A revision change** is a requested stored value that differs from what the row
  **stores** — not what it renders. Pinning a tracking claim to the very revision it shows
  is a change ("follow" becomes "hold"). It always creates a new row revision, even over a
  Draft, carrying the request's quantity / find number or the row's own; `forked: true`.
- **What a clear leaves.** A cleared claim becomes a tracking claim: it renders its source
  line's revision at T_R and moves only when a pull accepts a newer source. A cleared
  `new` row or substitute floats at `asOf`. Setting a pin that differs from the source
  line's revision starts rendering that revision's structure beneath the row; clearing it,
  or pinning the source line's revision, stops that, and any edits it hid render again.
- **A revision-only request equal to the stored state** (the same pin, or a clear of a row
  storing nothing) succeeds and writes nothing; `forked` is null. A retry after a lost
  response therefore succeeds.
- **A past `asOf`** is tolerated on an owned row unless the row has been revised since
  (`STALE_REVISION`).

**`autoClaim: true`** lets an `update` of a `base` edge claim and revise in one operation
instead of answering `CLAIM_REQUIRED`; the result says so with `claimed: true` and
`forked: null`. Because it claims, it then needs **exactly one of**
`childItemRevisionId` | `trackChildRevision: true` (the claim's revision choice) — but
only when the row turns out to be `base`. On a row the branch already owns, the flag is a
no-op (`claimed` null) and the revision fields mean what they mean on any `update`.

Guards are checked in this order:

1. `INVALID_REQUEST`: no id; nothing named; a quantity ≤ 0.
2. `REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED`: both `childItemRevisionId` and `trackChildRevision: true`
   (any row, before the lookup).
3. `NOT_FOUND`
4. `NOT_EDITABLE`: a nested row.
5. `CLAIM_REQUIRED`: a `base` row without `autoClaim`.
6. For an `autoClaim` claim of a `base` row: `REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` (neither choice),
   `INVALID_REQUEST` (a past `asOf`, as on `claim`), `REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH`,
   `INVALID_REQUEST` (another operation in the batch already changed the row's
   membership).
7. For an owned row: `NOT_SUPPLIED` (a tombstone), `STALE_REVISION` (a past `asOf`),
   `REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH`, `INVALID_REQUEST` (the row was already revised — or, for a
   revision change, had its membership changed — earlier in the batch).

### Choosing a child revision

A stored revision must always mean somebody chose it, so the operations that create or take
over a row treat `childItemRevisionId` as a deliberate choice, never a default:

| `op` | `childItemRevisionId` sent | `trackChildRevision: true` sent | Neither | Both |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claim` | **pins** the claimed row to it | row **tracks** the source line — the revision its unclaimed self would render, at T_R, moving when a pull accepts a newer source | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` |
| `convert-to-native` | **stamped** onto the native row | nothing stored; the native row **floats** at `asOf`, like an `add` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` |
| `add`, `replace` | **pins** the new row / substitute | ignored — blank already means track | the row **floats** at `asOf` (the default) | pins; the flag is ignored |
| `update` on an owned edge (with or without `autoClaim`) | **pins** it; a revision different from the stored one forks | **clears** the stored revision | keeps the stored revision | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` |
| `update` with `autoClaim: true`, on a `base` edge | claims and **pins** | claims and **tracks** | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` |
| `update` without `autoClaim`, on a `base` edge | `409 CLAIM_REQUIRED` | `409 CLAIM_REQUIRED` | `409 CLAIM_REQUIRED` | `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` |
| every other op | ignored | ignored | — | — |

- **There is no server-side "pin what I see".** To pin the revision the tree is showing, or
  to have a convert "keep what it shows", send back that row's own
  `detail.childItemRevisionId`. That includes converting a *pinned* claim that should stay
  pinned: nothing is retained implicitly.
- **The revision must belong to the row's child item** — for `claim`, the claimed line's
  child; for `replace`, the substitute; for `convert-to-native`, the converted row's.
  Otherwise `422 REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH`. A revision you cannot see answers the same code
  as one that does not exist, so the check is not an existence oracle. Lifecycle
  (Cancelled / Expired) is **not** screened at write time, because a revision can be
  cancelled long after it was chosen; the branch tree read and the comparison warn about
  it instead (`STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`).
- **Why `claim` has no default.** If claiming a line to change its quantity also pinned its
  revision as a side effect, it would silently also mean "never accept a new revision of
  this part" — two decisions, one of them invisible at the call site.
- **A pinned row can hide branch edits.** A pin on an assembly other than the revision its
  source line resolves to renders that revision's structure beneath it; see the
  [branch tree read](#operation/getBranchTree) and `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`.
- **Changing or clearing a revision after the row exists** is an `update`, which keeps the
  row's quantity and find number unless it sends new ones. `convert-to-native` may also
  stamp **any** revision of the child item, or switch to tracking. That is legitimate, and
  it is the severing path; `update` is the non-severing one.

### Addressing quirks worth knowing

- `update` accepts `ebomAssemblyId` **and has to**: a `base` row has no edge record, so
  that is the only id a client holds for the row whose update must come back
  `CLAIM_REQUIRED`. Without it the rejection could never be reached.
- `revert` accepts `ebomAssemblyId` for the mirror reason: a reverted row renders with no
  branch record (`ciId` is null), so a *second* revert — which must answer `NO_CLAIM` — cannot be
  addressed any other way.
- `replace` only works on eBOM-derived rows. A `new` row has a synthetic `new-…` edge
  key and no `Assembly__c` line, so replacing branch-added content is `update`, or
  `exclude` plus `add`.
- A row **hidden behind a pin** (see `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`), or on a parent
  revision nothing renders any more (see the [branch tree read](#operation/getBranchTree)),
  is addressable by
  `ciId` for `exclude`, `restore`, `revert` and `convert-to-native`, and by `assemblyCiId`
  for `update` (its new quantity / find number render once the pin no longer
  hides the row). An `update` addressed by `ebomAssemblyId` still answers `NOT_FOUND`
  for it. `claim` of a hidden line answers `NOT_FOUND` too, deliberately: a line that
  renders nowhere has nothing visible to claim.

## Access

Requires **create** on `Assembly_CI__c`, `CI__c`, `Assembly_CI_Rev__c`, `CI_Rev__c` and
`Branch_Member__c`, **and edit** on `Assembly_CI__c` and `Assembly_CI_Rev__c` (upserted or
edited in place), `CI_Rev__c` (updated when an operation freezes a predecessor) and
`Branch__c` (every write advances the branch's write clock). Create and edit are not the same
permission, and both are named so a partial grant is a 403 before anything is written.

200.description:
The batch report. Also returned when `atomic: false` and some operations failed — check
`failed` and each `results[].success`, not the status code.

forked.summary: An update that had to fork a frozen revision

autoClaimed.summary: An update that claimed a base line (autoClaim)

400.description:
`INVALID_REQUEST` — the body could not be read; or (under `atomic: true`) an operation
failed validation with a 400-mapped code: a missing required field, an unknown `op`, or
an operation that refuses a past `asOf`.

`ASOF_IN_FUTURE` — the batch's own `asOf` is later than now. An `asOf` that is not a
valid date-time fails the body parse, so it answers `INVALID_REQUEST`, not `ASOF_INVALID`.

Also `INVALID_REQUEST`, on `update`: none of `quantity`, `findNumber`,
`childItemRevisionId`, `trackChildRevision: true` sent; `autoClaim` claiming a `base`
edge at a past `asOf` (as a `claim` is; on an owned edge a past `asOf` stays
tolerated); and a second operation on a row that is refused by the batch-slot rules
(`already revised earlier in this same batch` / `that row already has a membership
change earlier in this same batch`). `"op": "set-revision"` is an unknown op.

value.message: That request could not be read. Check that the body is valid JSON and that every required value is supplied. (convert-to-native decides from the branch's CURRENT provenance, which a past asOf cannot report; send it without one)

409.description:
An atomic batch failed validation, and the first failure's code was a 409. The body
carries **every** failure in `failures[]`, not just the first — a caller fixing them one
round trip at a time is the behaviour this endpoint exists to avoid.

| code | Cause | Remedy |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAIM_REQUIRED` | a write targeted a `base` row | `claim` it first — or send the `update` with `autoClaim: true` and a revision choice |
| `ALREADY_CLAIMED` | `claim` on a row this branch already owns | edit it directly |
| `ALREADY_EXCLUDED` | `exclude` on a tombstoned row; or `convert-to-native` of one, which has no content to retain | `restore` it first |
| `NOT_EXCLUDED` | `restore` on a row that is not excluded | nothing to restore — your view is stale |
| `ALREADY_PRESENT` | `add` of a (parent, child) the branch already carries locally; or an op on a **replaced** row | edit the existing row; or act on the substitute |
| `NO_CLAIM` | `revert` on a row the branch asserts nothing about; `convert-to-native` on a row that is already `new` | nothing to undo or sever |
| `NOT_SUPPLIED` | `revert` on a row no source supplies — falling back would make it vanish | `exclude` instead |
| `STALE_REVISION` | an `update` at a past `asOf` against a revision superseded since | reload and retry |
| `NOT_EDITABLE` | the target is inside the subtree of a locally added or substituted assembly, or of a row holding a revision other than its source line's | only source-supplied content is editable |
| `CONCURRENT_WRITE` | another transaction holds this branch's write lock | send the same request again |

413.description:
`BATCH_TOO_LARGE` — more than 200 operations. Split the change.

`STRUCTURE_TOO_LARGE` — the branch is too large to validate the batch against in one
transaction. Nothing is written. Splitting the batch does not help; see
`StructureTooLarge`.

value.message: A single request can carry at most 200 operations. Split the change into smaller batches. (240 operations, maximum 200)

422.description:
Impossible against the model.

| code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `CYCLE_DETECTED` | the requested edge would make a child an ancestor of its own parent |
| `PARENT_NOT_IN_BRANCH` | `add` targeted a parent that is not part of this configuration |
| `EBOM_CYCLE` | the source eBOM already contains a cycle |
| `UNSUPPORTED_CI_TYPE` | a delta named a configuration item of a type this version does not support |
| `CI_IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED` | a configuration item has no data record, or one missing its identifying key — data corruption, never skipped |
| `CI_IDENTITY_COLLISION` | two configuration items resolve to one identity, so one of their deltas would be silently discarded |
| `PROVENANCE_INVALID` | a delta named a source that is not this branch's |
| `REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` | a `claim` or `convert-to-native` sent neither `childItemRevisionId` nor `trackChildRevision: true`, or sent both; an `update` sent both; an `update` with `autoClaim` that claims a `base` edge sent neither |
| `REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH` | a `childItemRevisionId` is not a revision of the operation's child item — or names no revision you can see |

`REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` is a property of the request alone, so it is checked once the
target is named and before any claim or exclusion state: a `claim` of an
already-claimed line that also chose nothing answers `REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED`, not
`ALREADY_CLAIMED`. `REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH` is checked after the state guards. On
`update`, "neither" is refused only once the lookup shows the row is `base` and
`autoClaim` is claiming it (message `update with autoClaim claims Assembly__c <edgeKey>,

post.summary: Cut a baseline over a branch
post.description:
Records the branch's full effective structure at one timepoint — **as that timepoint**.

## A baseline stores a timepoint, not rows

The cut writes one `Baseline__c` record carrying its resolution timepoint
(`resolutionTimePoint`), and nothing else about the content. Reading it back **replays the
resolution** at that timestamp, which is exact because the resolution is a pure function of
it and because nothing can ever land at or before a past T (every source acceptance and
every branch edit is stamped with the wall clock when it is written).

Storing the rows instead would cost one record per edge per cut — roughly 36 MB for an
18,000-edge BOM.

## The freeze is what makes the replay honest

A Draft row revision is edited **in place** by `update`. Replaying a timepoint would therefore
follow an edit made *after* the cut, and the baseline would change without anyone touching
it. So the cut freezes every revision the snapshot resolved to. From then on, every `update`
to those rows forks a new revision instead (and comes back `forked: true`).

## Two timestamps, and why they are not one

`resolutionTimePoint` is what the content was resolved at; `takenAt` is the wall-clock moment
of the cut. Kept apart, a correction to the server clock cannot change what a baseline
resolves to. The request names the timepoint `cutDateTime`; the response reports it as
`resolutionTimePoint`.

Both are reported **to the whole second** (milliseconds `.000`), matching what a later read
of the same record returns.

## Stored canary counts

The cut also stores how many rows are `claiming` and how many hold a chosen revision
(`hasChosenRevision`). Neither is returned here — there is no `pinnedCount` —
and both feed the baseline read's drift warnings.

## Excluded rows are not members

`memberCount` counts what the configuration *contains*, so tombstoned rows are not counted —
which means it is **not** the number of rows the tree endpoint renders. The baseline read
filters on the same rule, so the stored count stays comparable to a later read.

## Immutable from the insert

There is no draft-baseline state and no lock step: every update to a `Baseline__c` is refused
outright, and every hard delete too.

## Access

Requires **create** on `Baseline__c`, and **edit** on `CI_Rev__c` (the freeze) and
`Branch__c` (the cut advances the branch's write clock). Named separately because a partial grant would otherwise fail half way through the
cut — after the members resolve and before the freeze, the one state a baseline must never
be left in.

get.summary: Read the rows a baseline captured
get.description:
Re-resolves the branch at the baseline's stored `resolutionTimePoint` and returns the rows.

## `asOf` is refused, not ignored

Every other tree read on this API takes one, and a client that has been sending it to
`/branches/{id}/tree` will send it here. A baseline **pins its own timepoint**, so a second
one has nothing to answer — accepting it would give the same rows to every value and let a
caller believe they had asked a temporal question and got a temporal answer. Sending `asOf`
is a `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

Paging, `rowKey`s, `snapshot` and `compare` work exactly as on the
[branch tree read](#operation/getBranchTree). A baseline never changes, so `snapshot` only
matters with `compare`, where it pins the target.

## Differences from the branch read

- **Excluded rows are filtered out.** A tree read renders a tombstone so the editor can see
  what was removed; a baseline is the record of what the branch *contained*.
- **`edgeId`, `edgeKey` and `ciId` are null, and the per-row governing clock is
  collapsed** — every row's `governingTimestamp` is the baseline's own
  `resolutionTimePoint`, never null. A baseline row does not pretend to answer questions it
  cannot, and cannot be edited. `isReplaced` **is** populated: leaving it null would render
  a substituted part identically to an ordinary one.
- **No advice warnings.** A `MIXED_REVISION`, `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`,
  `MEMBER_ADD_COLLISION` or `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` warning is advice about a branch
  someone is still editing; a baseline is a record of a decision already taken, so none is
  raised here. `warnings` is empty except for `REDLINE_AMBIGUOUS` under `compare`.
- **Pinned rows reproduce exactly.** A row pinned to another revision re-resolves with that
  revision's `nested` structure beneath it and the source's lines suppressed, just as the
  branch read rendered it at the cut.
- **Pinned rows name who chose the revision.** A row with
  `hasChosenRevision: true` carries `revisionChosenById` and `revisionChosenAt`, the
  creator and creation time of the branch revision (`CI_Rev__c`) it resolves through —
  populated exactly as on the branch read. `wasClaimed` is evaluated as of the baseline's
  own timepoint.

## The drift canaries — reported by the findings

A drift canary compares counts over the **whole** baseline, which no page computes, so the
canaries are reported by [`GET /baselines/{baselineId}/findings`](#operation/getBaselineFindings),
not by this read.

| warningCode | What moved |
|---|---|
| `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` | the baseline re-derived a **different number of rows** than its cut recorded — a corrected release date, an edit to an already-released BOM |
| `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` | the same rows came back with a **different number of them `claiming`** — a claim severed or added since the cut. The row count cannot see this, because severing one moves no row |
| `BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT` | the same rows came back with a **different number of them holding a chosen revision** (`hasChosenRevision`) — a revision decision moved where neither the row count nor the claim count did |

All three **warn rather than throw**: the rows returned are still the honest answer for the
stored timepoint. The same canaries are raised on a comparison's baseline side.

None is complete, and the response does not pretend otherwise. An edit that changes only
a line's own fields, such as its quantity, moves no count.

get.summary: Preview the effect of accepting a newer eBOM revision
get.description:
Diffs the eBOM resolved at the source's current T_R against the eBOM resolved at the
candidate root revision's release date, and returns every difference as an individually
addressable entry.

**This call is pure.** It creates and modifies nothing — no branch edit, no row revision, no
source revision. Calling it twice with the same inputs against an unchanged
org returns identical entries, including identical `entryId` values and an identical
`diffFingerprint`. Only the read clock moves: `generatedAt`, and the `governingTimestamp` of
every state that answers to `asOf`.

**Not every entry is a decision.** Most are informational: the caller is being told what will
happen, not asked. Only `claim-orphaned` blocks a commit.

**Already current is not an error.** If the branch already resolves against the newest
released root revision, this returns `200` with `hasChanges: false` and an empty `entries`
array — correct for a read, where a write would throw.

## The correlation key — why a pull doesn't orphan every claim on every release

The two traversals are correlated on the BOM line's **`(Parent_Item__c, Item__c,
Secondary_Unique_Key__c)`** — the parent *item*, not the parent revision. **Not** on the
line's `edgeKey`.

This is the load-bearing decision of the whole feature. When a parent item revs, Propel
clones its entire BOM into new `Assembly__c` rows with new ids — so a branch that claimed a
line under rev-1 holds a line id that does not exist under rev-2. A join on `edgeKey` would
orphan every claimed edge and re-add every upstream line **on every single pull**. The
parent item does not move when its revision does, which is exactly what lets this key survive
the clone. `edgeKey` still identifies the edge *for display*; it just is not the join key.

`Secondary_Unique_Key__c` rather than `Find_Number__c` because find-number uniqueness is org
configuration, and a key built on it would give two orgs with identical data different diffs.

The key is **not unique** on one side when a parent item renders at two revisions in the
same tree, which is routine, because each occurrence of a pinned item renders its own
revision's structure. Revising an item copies each line's `Secondary_Unique_Key__c`
unchanged, so both revisions' copies of a line share one key. So within one side, edges at one key are
also told apart by their **parent revision**, the revision whose line each sits on, and a
pull over such a tree completes. The parent revision separates; it never joins, and it is
not part of the key: a branch edge and its source counterpart carry different parent
revisions once the source advances. Across the sides, edges at one key pair by equal
parent revision first, and then a lone edge left on each side pairs with the other — the
source advancing. A null parent revision never pairs by equality, only as a lone survivor;
`nested` rows pair in a second pass and never refuse. There is no tie-break on find number.

A live `replace` substitute borrows the key of the line it supersedes, and correlates
**through that line**. While upstream keeps the superseded line, the substitute
is `claim-retained` (`claimKind: replace`, `retargeted: false`, no actions; its `entryId`
derives from the superseded line's key and `candidate` is that line) on every pull, since
a substitute always diverges from the line it replaces. Only when upstream drops the
superseded line is it `claim-orphaned`. It is never judged against a line of its own new
child that upstream supplies at the borrowed key; that line is `member-added`. When
upstream adopts the substitution itself (drops the superseded line and adds a line of the
substitute's child at its position), the substitute is `claim-orphaned` and upstream's
line is `member-added`.

Where the join still cannot tell which upstream line corresponds to which branch line, the
pull answers `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` (422) rather than guess. The three shapes that raise
it, and their remedies, are listed under the 422 response.

## The two sides are deliberately asymmetric

- **current** — the branch resolved at the accepted T_R, *with* its own deltas overlaid.
- **candidate** — the **raw** upstream walk at the candidate T_R, with **no overlay at all**.

Overlaying the branch onto the candidate side would match nothing (the deltas are keyed on
line ids that do not exist under the new root) and would append every delta as an unmatched
local edge — which **resurrects the orphans**, correlating a claim on a removed line with the
branch's own edge so `claim-orphaned` is never raised. That entry is the only required
decision in the entire feature; silently losing it would make a commit that should block
succeed.

## Entry kinds

| kind | decision | availableActions | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source-version-advance` | informational | — | The root item revision advances; nothing structural beneath it changed. |
| `member-version-advance` | informational | — | An edge's child resolves to a newer released revision because T_R moved. |
| `member-added` | informational | — | The candidate adds an edge the branch has no native edge on. Enters automatically. |
| `member-removed` | informational | — | The candidate removes an edge the branch never claimed or replaced. Applies automatically. |
| `claim-retained` | informational | `accept-fields` (optional); none on a `replace` substitute | The branch's claim still differs from upstream; the branch wins and upstream is suppressed unless the commit accepts fields. `retargeted` distinguishes a suppressed **field value** from a suppressed **re-target**. |
| `claim-superseded` | informational | `release` (optional) | The branch's claim now *matches* what the candidate would natively produce. |
| `claim-orphaned` | **required** | `convert-to-native`, `remove` | The candidate removes an edge the branch **claimed or replaced**. **Blocks the commit.** |
| `member-add-collision` | informational | `accept-fields` (optional) | The candidate adds an edge whose correlation key coincides with a branch-**native** edge, and the two **differ**. The branch's content wins and is left untouched unless the commit accepts fields. |
| `member-add-converged` | informational | — | The same collision, except the candidate's quantity, find number **and** resolved child revision are all identical to the branch's own. The commit retires the branch's now-redundant local edge (`action: "retired"`); the position becomes ordinary `base` content. |

`member-add-collision` and `member-add-converged` are the same coincidence resolving two
ways. Converged requires all three of quantity, find number and resolved child revision to
match; any difference makes it a plain collision. Neither is ever a decision: on a
collision nothing is written and the branch's row stands, and on a converged entry the
commit retires the branch's local edge. A `claim-superseded` claim is never retired.

### Optional decisions

Three kinds offer **optional** per-field decisions. Their `decision` stays
`informational`; "optional" is a non-empty `availableActions` on an informational entry.
A pull has exactly one **required** kind, `claim-orphaned`, permanently, and an undecided
optional entry never blocks a commit — a preview with hundreds of entries and no
`claim-orphaned` still commits with zero decisions.

| kind | availableActions |
|---|---|
| `claim-retained` (any claim but a `replace` substitute — pinned or tracking, retargeted or not) | `["accept-fields"]` |
| `claim-retained` with `claimKind: replace` (a live substitute) | `[]` |
| `member-add-collision` | `["accept-fields"]` |
| `claim-superseded` | `["release"]` |
| `claim-orphaned` | `["convert-to-native", "remove"]` (required) |
| every other kind | `[]` |

`accept-fields` is offered on every such entry **without checking that some field could be
taken**. Where the only divergence is one the commit refuses (for example a collision
differing only on a find number the candidate line leaves blank), every `acceptedFields`
is refused `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; leave the entry undecided and the branch's value wins.
See the [pull commit](#operation/commitSiteBomPull) for what each field and value does.

`diffFingerprint` digests each entry's `availableActions` (and `revisionAdvances`). The
fingerprint does **not** cover the commit's `decisions[]`, so one preview's fingerprint
is valid for a commit with or without `acceptedFields`.

Preview entries and `warnings` describe the tree with **no optional decision taken**. An
accepted revision that lifts a post-pull pin is not previewed: a
`PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` warning for that pin no longer applies after such a commit,
and the lines entering, leaving or rendering again beneath it are not listed.

### `revisionAdvances`

`claim-retained` and `claim-superseded` carry `revisionAdvances`: `true` when a
**tracking** claim's rendered revision moves with this pull. No new entry kind is added,
so each position still has exactly one entry, and `member-version-advance` still means
`base` content only.

### Why a revision advance is never a decision

A revision is not an independently assertable value. Once you accept that the *line* exists,
which revision it resolves to is a deterministic output of the as-of traversal against T_R —
there is no alternative to offer. The way to hold a revision is to **pin** it — a `claim`
(or `add`, `replace`, `convert-to-native`) carrying a chosen `childItemRevisionId`, a
separate and deliberate act on the delta endpoint. A *tracking* claim holds nothing: it
follows the source's revision and moves with it.

A `base` row's advance is still never a decision. A *pinned* claim that upstream has moved
past can optionally take the candidate's revision through `accept-fields`
(`{"childItemRevisionId": "candidate"}`) or start tracking (`"release"`), keeping
everything else. A tracking claim's move is flagged with `revisionAdvances` on its
`claim-*` entry.

### Pins are judged against the tree *after* the pull

A row pinned to a revision other than its source line's renders that revision's structure
beneath it, and the source's lines there are suppressed. Which rows that applies to is
decided on the **post-pull** tree, not today's: a pin that upstream moves past becomes one
that suppresses structure, and a pin upstream converges onto, removes or moves stops being
one. Lines hidden behind a post-pull pin get no entry of their own. A branch edit such a pin
will hide is reported instead as a `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` warning — the same warning
the tree read will raise once the commit lands — because the preview is the last point at
which the caller can see that coming.

Pins are judged **per occurrence**, as the tree renders them. A line behind a
pin on one occurrence that another, unpinned occurrence of the same item still renders is
not hidden: it is reported there like any other line, as `member-added` when it is new.
A hidden-edit warning is raised once per pinned row and hidden item.

A live `replace` substitute hidden behind a post-pull pin gets no entry while hidden — only
a `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` naming the substitute's item — and is `claim-retained` once
the pin lifts. A branch `add` beneath a live substitute whose superseded line upstream
keeps renders after the commit, so it draws no hidden-edit warning.

A pinned claim whose line upstream re-revs is reported as `claim-retained` with
`retargeted: true`: the candidate would resolve the line to a newer revision, and the pin
wins. The commit leaves the pin in place — unless it carries an `accept-fields` decision
naming `childItemRevisionId`. With `candidate`, the pin moves to the candidate's revision,
equals the post-pull source line's, and stops rendering a pinned structure, so edits it
hid render again; the next pull that moves the line reports `retargeted: true` again.
With `release`, the claim stores no revision and becomes a tracking claim, never
`retargeted` again.

### Why upstream re-pointing an edge at a *different item* is two entries

The correlation key includes the child item, so it never correlates as one matched pair. It
decomposes into an independent `member-removed` (or `claim-orphaned`) and an independent
`member-added`. `retargeted: true` therefore means a different child **revision**, not a
different child item.

## Paging

Entries come in pages of `limit` (default 200). **Every `required` entry comes before any
informational one**, so the first page shows the blockers. `decision=required` returns the
required entries only — the whole set a commit must decide.

`summary`, `diffFingerprint` and `previewId` describe the **complete** diff on every page,
so a caller knows the size of the diff before paging, and can commit from any page. Follow
`page.nextCursor` for the rest. Each page continues after the last entry the previous page
returned, and the set of positions is fixed by the state the first page resolved, so no
entry is skipped or repeated while the diff stays the same. A Draft row's quantity or find
number edited in place between pages shows its newer value on later pages. If that edit
changes how an entry is reported, that one entry may be skipped or repeated, and
`diffFingerprint` and `previewId` change with it, so a commit carrying the earlier ones
answers `409 STALE_REVISION`.

`previewId` names this preview. Send it on the commit. Today it is checked like
`diffFingerprint`; a later version may hold a large diff server-side under it.

## Size

Pull preview and commit support structures up to 15 levels deep. A deeper structure may
answer `413 STRUCTURE_TOO_LARGE`.

**`202 Accepted` is reserved** for a later version that previews a very large pull as a
background job: the body would carry `status: accepted` and a `jobId`. This version always
answers `200` with `status: completed`, but a client should treat `status` as the outcome
rather than assume `200`.

## Target rows

Each entry tied to a row of the branch's current tree names it in `target.rowKey`, the
same key the [branch tree read](#operation/getBranchTree) uses, so a client can show the
entry in the tree. It is null for `member-added` (the branch has no such row yet) and for
`source-version-advance` (about the root).

## Access

**Gated on write, not read.** A read-only user is rejected before a pull is even previewed:
the preview requires exactly the create and edit grants that `pull` itself requires.
