get.summary: Compare a baseline against another configuration
get.description:
The same comparison as [`compareBranch`](#operation/compareBranch) — same right-hand types,
same kinds, same summary, same paging — with a **baseline** on the left instead of a
branch. `target.rowKey` names the row of the baseline's own tree read.

It exists because a baseline has to be able to sit on the left as well as the right: "what
has this branch done since we froze it?" and "what changed between these two builds?" are
both baseline-rooted questions, and neither can be asked by naming the baseline on the right
alone.

## `asOf` is refused here, not ignored

The left side is a baseline, so it resolves at the boundary its cut recorded. A second
clock has nothing to answer, and accepting one would let a caller believe they had asked a
temporal question and been given a temporal answer. Sending `asOf` is a
`400 INVALID_REQUEST` — the same reading
[`getBaselineTree`](#operation/getBaselineTree) takes. `rightAsOf` is still accepted,
unless the *right* side is a baseline too.

There is deliberately **no** `sources/{id}/comparison` and no eBOM-rooted left side. Both
can still be compared — as the right-hand side of a branch or baseline — and eBOM against
eBOM is already served by Propel's existing BOM Compare, which a third surface would
duplicate.

## Access

Read, not write, exactly as the branch-rooted endpoint. A baseline side is gated on
`Baseline__c` **and** `Branch__c`, because reading one resolves the branch behind it.

200.description: One page of the comparison, in the shape `compareBranch` returns — `left.kind` is `baseline`.

400.description:
`INVALID_REQUEST` — everything `compareBranch` refuses, **plus `asOf`**, which a
baseline left side cannot honour.

value.message: That request could not be read. Check that the body is valid JSON and that every required value is supplied. (asOf cannot be supplied for a baseline: a baseline resolves at its own recorded timepoint, and honouring a different one would not be that baseline)

404.description: `NOT_FOUND` — the path id names no baseline, `rightId` names nothing or the wrong object, or the path carries a trailing segment.

sessionToken.description:
Standard Salesforce OAuth 2.0 access token or session id, sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

BranchId.name: branchId
BranchId.description:
Id of the `Branch__c`. Returned as `branchId` from `POST /site-bom/site-boms`.

A malformed id, or a well-formed id of the wrong object, is a **404** — not a 500 and not a
403. The URI is what names the resource, so a path naming nothing is a path to nothing, and
the two tree endpoints therefore cannot be confused for each other by a caller that swaps a
branch id for a source id.

SourceId.name: sourceId
SourceId.description:
Id of the `Branch_Source__c`. Returned as **`sourceId`** from `POST /site-bom/site-boms`.

In this version a branch has exactly one source, an eBOM source. A source already names its
owning branch, which is why there is no separate `branchId` segment on these paths.

BaselineId.name: baselineId
BaselineId.description: Id of the `Baseline__c`, returned from the cut.

AsOf.name: asOf
AsOf.description:
The **branch** clock for this read. Defaults to the server clock when omitted; a future value
is `ASOF_IN_FUTURE` (400).

Governs the branch's own deltas, local content and substitutes. It does **not** govern
`base` content, which always resolves at T_R — that is the two-clock model, and passing
`asOf` to the source traversal is the single change that would quietly make a pinned Site BOM
float.

Accepts ISO-8601 (`2026-02-01T00:00:00Z`, `2026-02-01T00:00:00+05:30`) and the
space-separated form (`2026-02-01 03:04:05`, interpreted as GMT). A `+` offset is
repaired server-side after query-string decoding turns it into a space, so a legal ISO offset
does not fail in transport.

ParentRowKey.name: parentRowKey
ParentRowKey.description:
Read beneath this row instead of beneath the root: its children (`depth=1`) or its whole
subtree. The row itself is not returned. Use a `rowKey` exactly as a tree read issued it;
never compose or parse one.

A key that names no row in the state being read is `404 NOT_FOUND`. A key stays valid
across snapshots while its occurrence exists. Ignored beside `cursor`.

Depth.name: depth
Depth.description:
How many levels below the root (or below `parentRowKey`) to return: a positive integer, or
`all`. **Defaults to `all`**, so a request without `depth` returns the whole tree, paged. A grid expanding one level at a time sends `depth=1`.

Anything else is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`. Ignored beside `cursor`.

TreeLimit.name: limit
TreeLimit.description:
The most rows (or lines) one page returns: 1 to 2000, **default 500**. Anything else is
`400 INVALID_REQUEST`, never a silent fallback. A page may hold fewer rows than `limit` and
still have `hasMore: true`; rely on `hasMore`, never on a short page.

ListLimit.name: limit
ListLimit.description:
The most entries one page returns: 1 to 2000, **default 200**. Anything else is
`400 INVALID_REQUEST`, never a silent fallback. Rely on `page.hasMore`, never on a short
page.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description:
`page.nextCursor` from the previous page. The cursor carries the request it continues, so
every other parameter except `limit` is ignored beside it, and the page continues the state
the first one resolved; each endpoint says what an edit made between pages shows. Opaque; never expires; never parse it. A cursor this endpoint did
not issue for this record is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

Snapshot.name: snapshot
Snapshot.description:
The `snapshot` a previous tree read of this record returned. The read then resolves exactly
the rows that read did, even if the branch has been edited since, so children fetched
later fit the rows already on screen. `asOf` is ignored beside it, because the snapshot
carries its own.

Without it, the read resolves the current state at `asOf`. A snapshot pins which rows exist
and where they hang. A Draft row's quantity or find number edited in place since shows its
newer value. A snapshot never expires. One this endpoint
did not issue for this record is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

Compare.name: compare
Compare.description:
Adds a `redline` to every row, comparing this tree against a target:

- `source` — what this branch's own source supplies (branch tree read only).
- `baseline:{baselineId}` — a baseline, at its own recorded timepoint.
- `branch:{branchId}` — another branch, now.
- `ebom:{itemRevisionId}` — a released eBOM revision, at its release date.

On a live read the target resolves at the tree's own clock, so both describe one instant;
on a read at its own `asOf` it resolves now. A later page that sends the `snapshot` keeps
that pairing, including when it brings a different `compare`.

The target resolves exactly as the comparison's right side does with no `rightAsOf`. See
the [branch tree read](#operation/getBranchTree) for what each redline status means. Any
other form is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`; an id that names nothing, or the wrong object, is
`404 NOT_FOUND`. Omitted, every row's `redline` is null.

RightKind.name: rightKind
RightKind.description:
What the **right-hand** side of the comparison is. Required — a comparison against nothing
in particular is half a request, so a missing or unrecognised value is
`400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

- `branch` — another `Branch__c`, resolved with its own deltas overlaid.
- `baseline` — a `Baseline__c`, replayed at the boundary its cut recorded.
- `source` — a `Branch_Source__c`: what that source *supplies*, with no branch deltas
  folded in. This is the "what have I changed relative to upstream?" comparison.
- `ebom` — a released `Item_Revision__c`, walked raw, with no branch in the picture.

**Matched case-insensitively**, so `Branch` and `BRANCH` are both accepted. Send the
lower-case spelling: that is the published value, and it is what comes back in
`right.kind`.

RightId.name: rightId
RightId.description:
The record the right-hand side is. Its object must match `rightKind` —
`Branch__c`, `Baseline__c`, `Branch_Source__c` or `Item_Revision__c` respectively.

**Absent is a 400** (the caller described half a comparison); **present but naming nothing,
or naming another object, is a 404** (the caller named a resource that is not there). The
same split the path ids make.

RightAsOf.name: rightAsOf
RightAsOf.description:
The **right** side's read clock. `asOf` governs the left side; each side keeps its own pair
of clocks and never borrows the other's, which is why there are two parameters rather than
one. A branch read at now against a baseline frozen in March is two configurations at two
instants, and both are published on the response.

Defaults differ by side type — now for `branch` and `source`, and for `ebom` **that
revision's own release date**, since a raw eBOM walk has no acceptance to pin it and "the
eBOM of revision X" honestly means the eBOM as it stood when X was released.

**Refused for a `baseline` right side** (`400 INVALID_REQUEST`), which resolves at the
timepoint its cut recorded. Parsing and the future-value rule are `asOf`'s, unchanged.

IncludeUnchanged.name: includeUnchanged
IncludeUnchanged.description:
Emit a `member-unchanged` entry for every correlation key present and identical on both
sides, turning the response into the **complete merged BOM** — one entry per key across
both sides, which is what a side-by-side tree renders from a single call.

Defaults to `false`. **Only an explicit `true` (any case) turns it on**; anything else —
`includeUnchanged=1`, `=yes` — falls back to the default rather than raising, because the
fallback is the smaller response and loses no information: `summary.unchanged` carries the
count either way.

It costs no extra query. It does **not** raise the default `limit`, and it moves
`summary.total` and `summary.byKind`, which count entries emitted — see the endpoint
description.

Provenance.description:
Where a rendered row comes from. **Derived at read time, never stored** — `claiming` and
`new` differ only in whether the branch's row took over a source line.

The taxonomy has two axes — whether a record exists upstream, and whether the branch has
taken it over:

| | exists upstream (*source*) | has a branch record (*native*) |
|---|---|---|
| untouched | `base` | — |
| taken over | — | `claiming` |
| branch only | — | `new` |

- `base` — supplied by the source; no branch-owned record exists.
- `claiming` — a branch row that takes over a source row (copy-on-write ownership).
- `new` — branch-owned with no upstream counterpart ("native").
- `nested` — a descendant of a locally added or substituted assembly, rendered from that
  item's own eBOM; or a descendant of a **pinned** row whose chosen
  revision differs from its source line's, rendered from the pinned revision's eBOM in
  place of the source's lines. Read-only: every row in such a subtree carries
  `isEditable: false`, and the pull diff excludes them entirely. Appears on tree rows only,
  never in a diff entry's `MemberState`.

There is no `excluded` value: exclusion is tracked as a separate boolean alongside
provenance, never as a value of it. Nor is there a `claimed` value for a source row some
branch has taken over: that answer is branch-relative, so a source read with no branch
could not give it.

GoverningClock.description:
Which clock resolves this member. `source` is the pinned T_R (it only advances when a pull is
committed); `branch` is the caller's `asOf`. Both are legitimately in play at once, which is
what makes mixed revisions of one item possible.

CiKind.description:
Discriminator for the configuration-item type, and therefore for the shape of
`MemberState.detail`. `assembly-edge` is the only member type implemented; this enum is the
extension point where a future CI type is added.

`source` appears only on the root-level `source-version-advance` entry's `target` (and on the
root segment of every `path[]`), because that entry is about the source's root **item**
rather than an edge beneath it: it has no parent, no quantity and no find number.

rootItemRevisionId.description:
The **released** `Item_Revision__c` the Site BOM is built over. Its `Released_Date_Time__c`
becomes T_R.

siteBomName.description:
`Site_BOM__c.Name`. Required: a blank value is refused with `INVALID_REQUEST`, because an
Site BOM with a blank name would be named after its own record id, which nobody can search
for.

branchLabel.description: The branch's name, shown in every Salesforce list view and lookup, and its label.

branchId.description: The initial `Branch__c`. Use it on every `/branches/...` endpoint.

sourceId.description:
The `Branch_Source__c` linking the branch to its eBOM. **This is the `sourceId`** on
every `/sources/...` endpoint.

sourceRevisionId.description: The first acceptance (`Branch_Source_Rev__c`), which carries T_R.

StructureTree.description: The response body of the branch and source tree reads — one page of a branch's effective structure, or of a source's structure on its own.

asOf.description: The timepoint this tree was resolved at, echoed so the response is self-describing. Present even when the caller sent none, and taken from the `snapshot` when one was sent.

rootRevisionId.description: The root `Item_Revision__c` the structure hangs from.

sourceTimePoint.description: **T_R** — the source timepoint `base` rows resolve at.

snapshot.description:
Opaque name of the state this page resolved. Send it with child and page requests that
belong to the same view; see the `snapshot` parameter. Never parse it.

parentRowKey.description: The `parentRowKey` this page was read beneath; null for a read from the root.

compareTarget.description: What `compare` compared against, described as a comparison describes its right side. Null without `compare`, and always null on a source tree read.

rows.description: One page of rows in depth-first pre-order. Always present; empty rather than absent.

warnings.description:
Warnings about **rows in this page** only, each naming its row by `rowKey`. Always
present; empty rather than absent. Whole-configuration warnings are on the findings.

PageInfo.description: Where this page sits in the whole answer. There is deliberately no total count.

limit.description: The effective page size — the `limit` sent, or the default.

hasMore.description: True when another page follows. The only end-of-data signal; a short page is not one.

nextCursor.description: Send as `cursor` for the next page. Null exactly when `hasMore` is false. Opaque.

RowRedline.description:
How a row differs from the `compare` target — read as **this tree against the target**.
See the branch tree read for the full rules.

status.description:
- `added` — this tree has the row; the target does not.
- `removed` — the target has the row; this tree does not (rendered from the target,
  under every occurrence of its parent item in this tree), or this tree excluded it.
- `modified` — both have it, and `changedFields` differ.
- `unchanged` — both have it, identical.

changedFields.description: On `modified`, which of the three assertable values differ, in this fixed order; empty otherwise.

oldValues.description: On `modified`, the **target's** value of each changed field, keyed `quantity`, `findNumber` and `childItemRevisionId`; empty otherwise.

entryId.description: The `entryId` the comparison of the same pair gives this position, so the redline and the change list can be linked. Null on `unchanged` rows and on `REDLINE_AMBIGUOUS` rows. A row beneath a `removed` row is itself `removed`; it carries the comparison's entry for its position when the comparison reports that position as `member-added`, and is null when the comparison pairs that position elsewhere in this tree.

TreeRow.description:
One row of a resolved tree: one occurrence of one BOM line. Rows carry their own place in
the tree (`rowKey`, `parentRowKey`, `level`), so a client rebuilds the tree from any set of
pages by `parentRowKey`, and never by item id — one item can appear at several places.

rowKey.description:
Opaque, server-issued identity of this occurrence. It encodes the path from
the root, so two occurrences of one item have two keys. URL-safe, at most 16
characters per level, and **stable** across edits and snapshots while the occurrence
exists. A pull that accepts a new root revision replaces the source's BOM lines, so
it ends the occurrences that follow them: base rows, and claimed rows that follow
their source line, come back with new keys, while rows the branch added itself keep
theirs. Send it as `parentRowKey` to read beneath this row. Never compose or parse it.

parentRowKey.description: The `rowKey` of the row this one hangs beneath; **null for the root's children** (level 1).

level.description: Depth below the root — 1 for the root's children.

hasChildren.description: True when reading beneath this row would return at least one row. Under `compare`, true when either side has children.

ciId.description:
The `CI__c` the branch holds for this row — the id `exclude`, `restore`, `revert` and
`convert-to-native` take. **Null for a `base` row**, which has no branch
record, for a `nested` row, and on source and baseline rows.

warningCodes.description:
The codes of the row-level warnings about this row: `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`,
`MEMBER_ADD_COLLISION`, `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`, `NESTED_CYCLE_PRUNED`,
`REDLINE_AMBIGUOUS`. The full warning is in the response's `warnings`. Always present;
empty rather than absent.

redline.description: How this row differs from the `compare` target. Null without `compare`.

edgeId.description: The `Assembly_CI__c` edge. **Null for a `base` row** that no branch has claimed. Suppressed on baseline rows.

edgeKey.description:
The eBOM `Assembly__c` line id, or a synthetic key for branch-local content:
`new-{branchId}-{parentItemId}-{childItemId}` for an `add`, or
`replaces-{branchId}-{supersededEdgeKey}-{newChildItemId}` for a substitute. Suppressed
on baseline rows.

An edge key is identity and is never re-stamped. Treat it as opaque; never parse the
prefix.

A substitute always carries its own `replaces-…` key, even when its child item already
has its own line under the same parent: the two render as two rows, each under its own
key (see the branch tree read).

governingTimestamp.description:
T_R for a `base` row; `asOf` for every other row — `claiming`, `new` and `nested`.

A `claiming` row answers to `asOf` because this one field also governs the branch's own
quantity and find number, so it does not always name the clock that chose the row's
child revision (see `AssemblyEdgeDetail.childItemRevisionId`).

**On a baseline row it is collapsed, not suppressed:** every row carries the baseline's
own `resolutionTimePoint`. A frozen record honours exactly one timepoint, so a per-row
clock there would imply the reader could re-resolve at it — but the value is stated
rather than nulled, so one client code path renders baseline and tree rows alike.

sourceId.description: The `Branch_Source__c` this row came from. Null for a branch-local row.

isExcluded.description:
True for a tombstoned row. **Rendered by the branch tree read** so the editor can see
what was removed; **filtered out** by the baseline read.

isReplaced.description: True when this row stands in for another (`replace`). Populated on baseline rows too — a null would render a substituted part identically to an ordinary one.

isSuperseded.description:
True on an excluded row that a live substitute now stands in for: the other side of
`isReplaced`. `restore` refuses such a row with `ALREADY_PRESENT` until the substitute
is excluded, so a UI should not offer Restore on it. Defaults to `false`; always `false`
on baseline rows, which filter excluded rows out.

isEditable.description:
False on any row inside the subtree of a locally added or substituted assembly, or of a
row pinned to a revision other than its source line's. Every delta op
refuses those rows with `NOT_EDITABLE`, so a UI offering an action on one is offering an
action the API will reject.

isCollapsedCollision.description:
True when one BOM position is asserted by both the branch and its source and the two
render as a single row, with the branch's content winning. A tree read carries a
`MEMBER_ADD_COLLISION` warning alongside it.

Defaults to `false`. Populated on baseline rows too, where — because a baseline
forwards drift warnings only — it is the sole signal of the collapse.

hasChosenRevision.description:
True when this row stores a child revision somebody **chose**: an `add`
or `replace` that sent `childItemRevisionId`, a `claim` that pinned, a
`convert-to-native` that stamped, or an `update` that pinned. Never null. This is
what "pinned" means in this API.

It follows the explicit choice only, never what the row happens to render:

- A tracking claim or a floating row is `false`, even when it resolves to exactly the
  revision a pin would have named.
- A pin **equal** to its source line's revision is `true`, although it renders no
  pinned structure.
- A floating `new` row that renders a pinned structure because the read clock moved
  past T_R is `false`: nobody chose it.
- Tombstones, `nested` rows and every row of a source tree are `false`.

The structural sense — a held revision that differs from its source line's, rendering
that revision's structure — is a different signal, surfaced only through
`PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` and `isEditable` on the rows beneath. Never derive one from
the other. Populated on baseline rows too.

wasClaimed.description:
True on a `new` row that once claimed a source row, and that `convert-to-native`
flipped from `claiming` to `new`. The provenance says the row is the
branch's own now. This says it did not start that way, which an audit of a released
configuration needs to see. Never null.

`false` on a row that claims now, so it is never combined with `isClaimed`, and on a
read dated before the conversion. A display fact about one row's history,
deliberately **not** a provenance value. Populated on baseline rows too, evaluated as of
the baseline's own timepoint. Every convert makes a stamp-or-track choice, so a
`wasClaimed` row may or may not have `hasChosenRevision`.

revisionChosenById.description:
The user Id of whoever chose the revision the row stores: the user whose `claim`,
`add`, `replace`, `update` or `convert-to-native` set or changed it. Populated wherever
`hasChosenRevision` is true — on live tree reads and baseline rows alike — and null
wherever it is false.

An edit that keeps the stored revision never changes it, even when that edit forks a
new branch revision (the first quantity edit after a baseline cut always does). Only a
change of the stored revision names a new chooser.

revisionChosenAt.description:
When the revision was chosen — the write time of the request that set or changed it
— to the whole second. Null exactly where `revisionChosenById` is.

TreeWarning.description:
A condition worth telling the user about that does **not** block the read. Shared by the tree
reads, the findings, the pull preview and the comparisons.

A tree read carries only the warnings about the rows it returns; the
[findings](#operation/getBranchFindings) carry every warning about the whole configuration.

The key is **`warningCode`**, matching the existing Site BOM convention — never `code`, which
this API reserves for the error body.

warningCode.description:
The complete vocabulary.

- `MIXED_REVISION` — one item rendered at more than one revision in the same tree,
  because two clocks are in play. Legal and expected; warned, never blocked. Each
  occurrence renders its own revision's structure. A whole-configuration finding: on
  the branch findings, the pull preview and a comparison's sides, never on a tree
  read, whose page may hold only one of the revisions.
- `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT` — a baseline re-derived a different **row count** than its cut
  recorded.
- `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` — a baseline re-derived a different number of **`claiming`**
  rows than its cut recorded. Separate from the count drift because severing a claim
  moves no row: the same rows come back, one of them no longer a claim.
- `NESTED_CYCLE_PRUNED` — the structure of a locally added or substituted assembly, or
  of a pinned revision, was dropped because walking it reached a cycle. The rest of the
  tree is still returned; when pins were involved it falls back to the unsuppressed
  source structure, and raises no `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`.
- `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` — some of the branch's edits take no effect,
  because a pinned row's own revision structure replaced the source lines they sit on:
  a claim, exclusion, update or substitute on a suppressed line (and on no line still
  rendered elsewhere), or an `add` under an item only the suppressed structure
  supplied. Not raised for an exclusion of a line upstream has already removed (what
  `remove` leaves on a `claim-orphaned` line): it removes nothing that exists.
  Rendered, never refused. Raised once per pinned row and hidden item: on the branch
  tree read (on the pinned row, whose `rowKey` it carries, with the hidden item in
  `itemId`), on the findings, and on the pull preview, where it describes
  the tree **after** the commit (with no optional decision taken).
  The remedy is an `update` on the pinned row: clear it with
  `trackChildRevision: true`, or pin it to the source line's own revision. Either keeps
  the row's quantity and find number, and the hidden edits render again.
- `MEMBER_ADD_COLLISION` — one BOM position was asserted by **both** the branch and its
  source, and the branch's content won. The two rows render as one, carrying
  `isCollapsedCollision: true`. Not raised once a pull has retired a *converged* local
  add, because only the source asserts the position from then on.
- `COMPARE_ROOTS_DIFFER` — a comparison's two sides are rooted at different **items**,
  so they have no members in common and every entry is an addition or a removal for
  that reason alone. The comparison still answers; refusing would be the wrong call for
  a read. Comparison responses only, where it is reported on **`leftWarnings`** — it is
  about the pair rather than either side, the response has two warning lists and no
  third, and the left is the side the caller addressed by path. It carries no `itemId`
  and no revisions: there is no single item it is about, and `left` / `right` already
  publish both roots.
- `BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT` — a baseline re-derived a different number of rows
  **holding a chosen revision** (`hasChosenRevision`) than its cut recorded. The count
  covers contained members, excluding tombstones, `nested` rows and edits hidden behind
  a pin. It catches a revision decision moving where no row count or claim count moved.
  Raised only where a baseline is re-resolved: the baseline findings, and a
  comparison's baseline side. It carries no `itemId` and empty arrays, like the other
  drift codes.
- `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` — a row's explicitly stored child revision (a
  pinned `add` / `replace`, a pinned claim, a stamped `convert-to-native`, a pinning
  `update`) has since been **Cancelled or Expired**. The row still renders that
  revision: nothing is substituted, and the read does not fail. `message` is the Custom
  Label `CM_Warn_STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`.

  One warning per row, not deduplicated by item, in a deterministic order. `itemId` is
  the row's child item and `itemRevisionIds` holds exactly the stored dead revision.
  Never raised by a row that stores no revision (a tracking claim or convert, a floating
  `new` row), by a tombstone, or by an edit hidden behind a pin. On a dead pin with
  nested structure, it names the pinned row, not the rows beneath it. A user who cannot
  see the stored revision under sharing gets no warning. Raised on the branch tree read
  (on the row), on the branch findings, and on both sides of a comparison (branch and
  baseline sides); **not** on the baseline tree read or the pull preview.
- `REDLINE_AMBIGUOUS` — under `compare`, the correlation join could not tell
  which row of this tree pairs with which row of the target at one position, so the
  rows are shown unpaired (`added` and `removed`) instead of refusing the read. One
  warning per such row, carrying its `rowKey`. The
  [comparison](#operation/compareBranch) of the same pair answers
  `422 AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` and its remedies apply. Tree reads with `compare` only.

message.description: Human-readable, from a Custom Label. Translated; never parse it.

rowKey.description:
The row the warning is about, on a tree read and on the findings:
`STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`, `MEMBER_ADD_COLLISION`, `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` (the
pinned row), `NESTED_CYCLE_PRUNED` and `REDLINE_AMBIGUOUS`. Null on `MIXED_REVISION`,
the drift codes and `COMPARE_ROOTS_DIFFER`, and on every pull-preview and comparison
warning.

itemId.description:
Present on `MIXED_REVISION` — the item rendered at more than one revision — on
`MEMBER_ADD_COLLISION`, naming the child item whose position collapsed, and on
`PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`, naming the child item of the edited line a pinned
revision's structure replaced (or, on a pull preview, will replace), and on
`STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`, naming the child item of the row holding the dead revision.
Null on the drift codes and `COMPARE_ROOTS_DIFFER`.

itemRevisionIds.description:
Present on `MIXED_REVISION` — the revisions in play — and on
`PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS`, where it holds the revision of the pinned row whose
structure hid the edit (that row's `detail.childItemRevisionId`), with
`governingTimestamps` left empty; and on `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`, where it holds
exactly one id, the Cancelled or Expired stored revision, with `governingTimestamps`
left empty. Every other code leaves it empty.

governingTimestamps.description: Present on `MIXED_REVISION` — the clock that governed each, positionally aligned with `itemRevisionIds`.

atomic.description:
All-or-nothing when true. **A null is treated as `true`** — the safer contract wins the
default, so a caller who did not think about the failure mode gets all-or-nothing rather
than a half-applied branch.

asOf.description:
Resolves the branch **once** for the whole batch; every operation then validates against
that one snapshot, so a batch cannot see the tree shift underneath it halfway through.

Defaults to the server clock; never accepted in the future. A **past** value means
"validate against the configuration as it stood then" — it never dates the write. Several
operations refuse a past value outright; see the endpoint description.

operations.description: At most 200 — beyond that, `BATCH_TOO_LARGE` (413), refused before anything is resolved.

DeltaOperation.description:
One operation. The shape is a **union across all eight operations** rather than a separate shape per
operation, because the batch arrives as one JSON array. `op` selects which fields are
meaningful, and each operation validates its own required fields — an `add` with no
`parentItemId` is that operation's error to raise, not a deserialisation failure.

Unknown keys are **silently ignored** (the deserialiser is lenient), so a *mistyped* field
name reads as a null id. `rootItemRevisionld` with an `l` will answer `NOT_FOUND`, not a
schema error.

op.description:
Matched case-insensitively. An unknown value is a **per-operation** validation failure (`INVALID_REQUEST`), not an exception — one mistyped name in a batch of 200 must not read as a server fault.

There is no `set-revision`: changing or clearing a stored revision is an `update`.
`set-revision` answers `INVALID_REQUEST` (`unknown op set-revision`).

clientRef.description:
Opaque caller token, echoed verbatim on this operation's result. Set it to correlate
results with a UI row; the server never interprets it. Correlating on order alone breaks
the moment anything is reordered, and on `clientRef` alone breaks when you do not set it
— so `index` is stated too.

ebomAssemblyId.description:
The eBOM `Assembly__c` line. Used by: `claim`, `exclude`, `update` (the `CLAIM_REQUIRED` path, and the `autoClaim` path), `revert` (the second-revert path).

Never finds a row hidden behind a pin: an `update` addressed by it answers `NOT_FOUND`
there.

assemblyCiId.description:
An existing `Assembly_CI__c` edge to `update`. The ordinary form.

The **request** keeps this name while the result publishes the same id as `edgeId`.
Not an oversight: a request carries every operation's fields in one flat shape, and
the operation an id belongs to is known only after `op` is read — so a request field
cannot be grouped per configuration-item type the way a response's can.

It also finds a row hidden behind a pin, which `ebomAssemblyId` never does.

replacedEbomAssemblyId.description: `replace` only — the eBOM line being superseded. Must be an eBOM-derived row; a branch-local row cannot be replaced.

newChildItemId.description: `replace` only — the substitute part. Its revision **floats** at the read clock unless `childItemRevisionId` pins it.

quantity.description:
Used by `update`, `add`, `replace`. On `update`, omitted keeps the row's value, and
≤ 0 answers `INVALID_REQUEST` (use `exclude` to remove a row).

findNumber.description: Used by `update`, `add`, `replace`. On `update`, omitted keeps the row's value.

childItemRevisionId.description:
An explicit child `Item_Revision__c` for the row this operation creates, takes over or
revises — `add`, `replace`, `claim`, `convert-to-native` and `update`. Ignored on every
other operation.

A value means "use exactly this revision, whatever the clock says": a deliberate pin,
never a default. It must be a revision **of the operation's child item** — the claimed
line's child for `claim`, the substitute for `replace`, the converted row's child for
`convert-to-native` — or the operation answers `422 REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH` (also the
answer for an id naming no revision you can see).

- On `add` and `replace`, **blank means track**, and is the default: the row floats at
  the read clock.
- On `claim` and `convert-to-native`, blank is **not a choice on its own**: send either
  this or `trackChildRevision: true` — exactly one — or the operation answers
  `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED`.

There is no server-side "pin current". To pin what the tree shows, or to have a convert
keep what it shows, send back that row's `detail.childItemRevisionId`.

- On `update` of an owned row, it **pins** the row to this revision, validated against
  the row's own child item. One different from the revision the row **stores** is a
  revision change and always forks; an equal one changes nothing. Omitted (or null)
  keeps the stored revision — clearing is `trackChildRevision: true`, never a null
  here.
- On `update` with `autoClaim: true` of a `base` edge, it pins the claim the update
  performs.
- Sent together with `trackChildRevision: true` on `update`:
  `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED`.

trackChildRevision.description:
`claim`, `convert-to-native` and `update`: `true` stores **no** revision.
`false` and null both mean "not chosen".

- On `claim`, the row **follows the source**: it keeps rendering exactly the revision its
  unclaimed self would, at the accepted source's T_R, and moves when a pull accepts a
  newer source. It does not float at the read clock.
- On `convert-to-native`, the row has no source left to follow, so it **floats at the
  read clock**, exactly like an `add`.

- On `update` of an owned row, `true` **clears** the stored revision: a
  cleared claim follows its source line at T_R, a cleared `new` row or substitute floats
  at the read clock. Clearing a row that stores a revision always forks; clearing one
  that stores none changes nothing. **It does clear a pin** — a client that sends
  `trackChildRevision: true` on every `update` will un-pin every pinned row it touches.
- On `update` with `autoClaim: true` of a `base` edge, `true` claims and tracks.

`claim` and `convert-to-native` must carry exactly one of this (`true`) and
`childItemRevisionId`; neither, or both, is `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED`. `update`
may carry neither (keep), but both is `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED`. **Ignored, not
refused, on every other operation** — `add` and `replace` already track when
`childItemRevisionId` is blank, and refusing it would make one shared client payload
shape invalid for them.

autoClaim.description:
`update` only. When `true`, an update of a `base` edge **claims it and
revises it in one operation**, instead of answering `409 CLAIM_REQUIRED` — otherwise
two requests, because a batch validates every operation against one pre-batch
snapshot.

- **The implicit claim makes the same revision choice `claim` does.** When the row is
  `base`, send exactly one of `trackChildRevision: true` or `childItemRevisionId`.
  `trackChildRevision: true` is the expected case: the row keeps following its source
  line. `childItemRevisionId` claims and pins. Neither answers
  `422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` (checked after the row is looked up, so a missing row
  answers `NOT_FOUND` instead); both answers it on any row, before the lookup. There is
  no default, for the reason `claim` has none.
- **No quantity or find number is needed** on a `base` row: `autoClaim` +
  `trackChildRevision: true` alone is a plain tracking claim with the line's own
  quantity and find number.
- **The result reports the claim.** `DeltaResult.claimed` is `true` and `forked` is
  null (a claim's first revision is not a fork). `CLAIM_REQUIRED` would have disclosed
  the eBOM line before the fact; this discloses it after.
- **On an edge the branch already owns**, the flag is a no-op: `claimed` stays null and
  the revision fields mean what they mean on any `update` — neither keeps the stored
  revision, `childItemRevisionId` pins (a different one forks), and
  `trackChildRevision: true` **clears** the stored revision. To keep whatever an owned
  row stores, omit both revision fields.
- **It bypasses no other guard.** These all still refuse the operation:
  - `NOT_EDITABLE` on a nested row, `NOT_SUPPLIED` on an excluded one, `STALE_REVISION`
  - a non-positive quantity, or a second operation on the same edge in the batch
  - every guard `claim` applies: a past `asOf` on a `base` edge (`INVALID_REQUEST`),
    `REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH`, and a membership change on the same row earlier in the
    batch. So `[replace(L, X), update(L, autoClaim)]` and
    `[claim(L), update(L, autoClaim)]` are refused `INVALID_REQUEST`.
  - On an edge the branch already owns, no claim happens, so a past `asOf` stays
    tolerated as on plain `update`.
- A row hidden behind a pin is found by `assemblyCiId` only (it is owned, so the flag
  is a no-op there); by `ebomAssemblyId` it answers `NOT_FOUND`.

`false` and null both mean off: `CLAIM_REQUIRED`, still carrying the eBOM line.
Ignored, not refused, on every other operation.

atomic.description: Echoed, so the response says which contract it was written under.

asOf.description:
The timepoint the whole batch resolved against. It matters more here than on a read — the
caller may have sent none at all, and this is the only way to learn which server clock
the batch actually used.

applied.description: Count of operations that succeeded. Stated so a client can act on the summary without walking `results`.

results.description: One entry per requested operation, **in request order**, success or failure.

snapshot.description:
The branch's state **after** this batch, as a tree read would name it.
Read with it to see your own writes and nothing later. Present even when nothing was
applied, naming the unchanged state.

invalidatedParentRowKeys.description:
The `rowKey`s of rows whose children a client should read again, because a row beneath
them was added, removed or changed by this batch. An empty string stands
for the root. Empty when nothing was applied. Always present.

index.description: Zero-based position of this operation in the request.

clientRef.description: Your own token, echoed verbatim. Null when you set none.

errorCode.description:
The error code on failure, null on success. Note the key is **`errorCode`** here, inside
a per-operation result — the top-level *error body* uses `code`.

The values are `RestError.code`'s vocabulary — that enum is the complete list. Left a
plain string here so a code added to the vocabulary never makes a batch result fail
validation in an older client.

message.description: Human-readable, from a Custom Label. Never parsed.

ciId.description: The `CI__c` this operation created or acted on.

edgeId.description:
The edge this operation created or acted on, in its CI type's own vocabulary — an
`Assembly_CI__c` for the assembly type. The same value, under the same name, that
`TreeRow.edgeId` publishes. The REQUEST field `assemblyCiId` is a different field
and keeps its name.

forked.description:
True when an `update` had to allocate a **new** row revision rather than edit one in
place — because a baseline had frozen it, or because the update changed the stored
child revision, which always forks. Surfaced because your next read will
show a revision number you did not ask for.

**Deliberately not defaulted.** Only `update` forks. `null` means *not applicable*
(there was nothing to fork on a `claim` or an `exclude`); `false` means *this write could
have forked and did not*. A client must treat them differently, so the field must be able
to say both.

Also `null` on an `update` that auto-claimed (`claimed: true`) — it minted a claim's
first revision, exactly as `claim` does — and on a revision-only `update` that the row
already satisfied, which writes nothing.

claimed.description:
`true` when this operation took ownership of a `base` edge on the caller's behalf,
which only an `update` sent with `autoClaim: true` can do. Nothing else in
the response would say so: `edgeId` is populated either way.

**Never `false`.** It is `null` whenever no claim was performed: `autoClaim` off, an
`autoClaim` on an edge the branch already owned, a failure, and every other operation.

label.description: `Baseline__c.Name`. Required: a missing or blank label is a 400. Over 80 characters is a 400, not a 500.

cutDateTime.description:
Optional; defaults to the server clock. Becomes `resolutionTimePoint` in the response.
**Never accepted in the future** (`ASOF_IN_FUTURE`) — a baseline of content that does not
exist yet is not a baseline.

resolutionTimePoint.description: What the baseline resolves against. **Stamped once, never re-derived.** Reported to the whole second, as a later read of the same record returns it.

takenAt.description: The wall-clock moment of the cut. Kept apart from `resolutionTimePoint` so a clock correction cannot change what a baseline resolves to. Reported to the whole second.

memberCount.description:
How many rows the cut resolved, **excluding tombstones**. This is the count of what the
configuration *contains*, not the count of rows the tree endpoint renders. Also the
canary behind `BASELINE_COUNT_DRIFT`; `BASELINE_PROVENANCE_DRIFT` is fed by the
`claiming`-row count recorded alongside it.

The cut also records a count of rows holding a chosen revision, feeding
`BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT`. Like the `claiming` count, it is stored and **not**
returned here: there is no `pinnedCount`.

resolutionTimePoint.description: What the baseline resolved against when it was cut.

snapshot.description: As on `StructureTree`. A baseline never changes, so it matters only with `compare`, where it pins the target.

parentRowKey.description: The `parentRowKey` this page was read beneath; null for a read from the root.

rows.description:
One page of the re-resolved rows, reusing the tree shape so clients render both the
same way — with `edgeId`, `edgeKey` and `ciId` nulled, `governingTimestamp`
collapsed onto this baseline's own `resolutionTimePoint`, and excluded rows filtered
out.

warnings.description:
Empty, except for `REDLINE_AMBIGUOUS` under `compare`. Always present. The drift
canaries are on the [baseline findings](#operation/getBaselineFindings).
Mixed-revision, collision, hidden-edit and `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` warnings are
advice about a branch, not a baseline, and are not raised. (A comparison's baseline
side does carry `STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`.)

FlattenedStructure.description: One page of a flattened view — one line per part, quantities multiplied down the tree and summed.

asOf.description: The timepoint resolved — the caller's `asOf`, the server clock, or a baseline's own timepoint.

sourceTimePoint.description: **T_R** — the source timepoint `base` content resolved at.

jobId.description: Reserved; always null in this version. Names the background job when `status` is `accepted`.

lines.description: Always present; empty rather than absent.

FlattenedLine.description: One part at one revision and secondary unique key, with its total quantity per build of the root.

childItemRevisionId.description: The revision every occurrence on this line renders. Null for a floating row whose item has nothing released at the read clock.

secondaryUniqueKey.description: The BOM lines' secondary unique key; null where the lines carry none. Lines of one part at one revision with different keys stay separate, as in the eBOM flattened view.

totalQuantity.description: The part's quantity multiplied down each occurrence path from the root, summed over every occurrence on this line.

occurrences.description: How many places in the tree contribute to this line.

warningCodes.description: `MIXED_REVISION` when the same part also appears at another revision, on another line. Always present.

Findings.description: One page of the warnings about a whole configuration — a branch's, or a baseline's drift.

asOf.description: The timepoint resolved — the caller's `asOf`, the server clock, or a baseline's own timepoint.

jobId.description: Reserved; always null in this version.

findings.description: Always present; empty is the healthy answer.

OutputStatus.description:
Whether the output in this response is complete (`completed`, with HTTP 200 or 201), or was
accepted as a background job (`accepted`, with HTTP 202 and a `jobId`). **This version
always answers `completed`.** `accepted` is reserved so a later version can process very
large configurations in the background without breaking a client that already checks it.

EntryKind.description:
What kind of change the diff found. Deliberately framed in generic framework terms (source /
member / claim) rather than Site BOM terms, so the taxonomy survives a second
configuration-item type. See the preview endpoint's table for the full catalog.

Decision.description:
Whether this entry needs the caller to decide anything. **Only two values.** `required`
means `claim-orphaned` only — a pull has exactly one required kind, and disposing an
orphaned claim is its only mandatory decision point. An `informational` entry may still
**offer** an optional action in `availableActions` (`accept-fields`, `release`);
undecided, its outcome is the default — the branch's value wins.

Action.description:
An action the commit endpoint can apply. A decision is valid only when its entry
**offers** the action in `availableActions`; otherwise `INVALID_REQUEST`. Matched
case-insensitively; echoed in its canonical lowercase spelling.

- `convert-to-native` — `claim-orphaned` only. Sever the claim's provenance link, keeping
  its branch-owned content, which then resolves on the branch clock. ("Native" is the
  framework's existing term for branch-owned content with no upstream provenance.)
- `remove` — `claim-orphaned` only. Append a deletion marker (an exclude delta). Nothing
  is hard-deleted.
- `accept-fields` — optional, on `claim-retained` (not a `replace` substitute) and
  `member-add-collision`. Takes the fields named in `acceptedFields`; the rest
  keep the branch's values. Compiles to exactly **one** `update` on the entry's edge.
- `release` — optional, on `claim-superseded` only, where the claim now
  matches upstream anyway. A `revert` of the claim, pinned or tracking alike: the branch
  stops owning the row, which renders upstream's line. Takes no `acceptedFields`.

`retired` appears only in `AppliedEntry.action`, for a `member-add-converged` entry the
commit retired automatically; it is never sent.

status.description:
`completed` — the preview is computed and every field below is filled in. Always
`completed` in this version. `accepted` (with HTTP 202 and a `jobId`) is reserved for a
background preview.

jobId.description: Reserved; always null in this version.

branchId.description: The owning branch, denormalised for display.

branchLabel.description: The branch's label, or its name when the label is blank.

sourceType.description: Always `Ebom` in this version; `Pull` (branch-to-branch) is reserved for a later version.

candidateSourceVersion.description: Absent or null when `hasChanges` is false and no newer revision exists to preview.

hasChanges.description:
False when the branch already resolves against the candidate, or there is no newer
released revision. `entries` is empty in that case. **Not an error condition.**

entries.description:
One page of the differences found: every `required` entry before any informational
one, each tier in a stable, deterministic order. Always present; empty rather than
absent.

warnings.description:
Non-blocking conditions about what would render *after* the pull (with no optional decision taken) — typically `MIXED_REVISION`, and `PINNED_SUBTREE_HIDES_EDITS` for a branch edit a post-pull pin will hide. Always present; empty rather than absent.

`STORED_REVISION_RETIRED` is not raised here; the branch tree read and the comparison
raise it.

previewId.description:
Opaque name of this preview — the candidate, the branch state it was taken against, and
the diff. The same on every page, unless a Draft row edited in place between pages
changes the diff; it then changes with `diffFingerprint`, and a commit carrying the
earlier one answers `409 STALE_REVISION`. Send it on the commit. Never parse it.

diffFingerprint.description:
Opaque `sha256:`-prefixed digest of the inputs and the **complete** resolved entry set
(not one page). Echo it back on commit; a mismatch means the world moved in
between and fails fast with `STALE_REVISION`.

It covers a **clock-free** projection of the entries, because a claiming row's
`governingTimestamp` *is* the read clock — folding it in would make every commit stale on
arrival. The projection includes each entry's `availableActions` and
`revisionAdvances`. It does **not** cover the commit's `decisions[]`.

generatedAt.description: Server clock at computation time. Informational; **not** a resolution input, and not part of the fingerprint.

SourceVersionRef.description:
One version of a source — the accepted eBOM root revision plus the clock that governs
traversal beneath it.

`rootItemRevisionId`, `rootItemNumber` and `rootRevisionLabel` name an `Item_Revision__c`,
because every source in this version is an eBOM source. A later source type would add an
alternative shape, discriminated on `PullPreview.sourceType` — an additive change.

sourceRevisionId.description: The `Branch_Source_Rev__c` recording this acceptance. **Null on `candidateSourceVersion`**, which does not exist until a commit creates it.

resolutionTimestamp.description:
**T_R** — the timestamp the eBOM traversal resolves against. Stamped once at acceptance
from the root revision's release date and read thereafter, never re-derived. Deriving it
per-read would let a later corrected or backdated approval silently rewrite history.

acceptedAt.description: Wall-clock moment the acceptance was committed, kept distinct from `resolutionTimestamp`. Null on `candidateSourceVersion`.

DiffSummary.description: Counts over the **whole** diff, on every page, so a caller can render "N informational, M requiring a decision" without paging through `entries`.

required.description: Entries that will block a commit until given an explicit decision. Only `claim-orphaned` counts here.

byKind.description: Count per `EntryKind`, keyed by kind. Kinds with no entries are omitted.

entryId.description:
Stable, opaque handle, passed back to the commit endpoint to attach a decision. A
**deterministic hash of `kind` plus the correlation key** — never a database Id, never
positional, never generated — so recomputing the same diff yields the same ids. Treat it
as opaque; do not parse it.

availableActions.description:
The decisions the commit accepts for this entry. Always present.

| kind | availableActions |
|---|---|
| `claim-orphaned` | `["convert-to-native", "remove"]` — required |
| `claim-retained` (not a `replace` substitute) | `["accept-fields"]` — optional |
| `claim-retained` with `claimKind: replace` | `[]` |
| `member-add-collision` | `["accept-fields"]` — optional |
| `claim-superseded` | `["release"]` — optional |
| every other kind | `[]` |

An optional action never changes `decision` (it stays `informational`) or
`summary.required`. `accept-fields` is offered without checking that some field could
legally be taken.

retargeted.description:
**Present only on `claim-retained`; `null` on every other kind** (deliberately not
defaulted — a `false` would assert something about a kind for which the question is
meaningless).

True when the suppressed upstream change was a **re-target**: the candidate would resolve
this edge to a different child *revision* than the claim renders — the shape a
**pinned** claim takes when upstream re-revs its line. False when only field
values (quantity, find number) were suppressed. Lets a caller filter for the
higher-stakes case — a branch silently keeping a superseded revision after upstream moved
on — without parsing `message`.

The child *revision*, not the child *item*: see the endpoint description. Always
`false` for a `replace` substitute, and never `true` on a tracking claim.
Only a retargeted pinned claim's revision **diverges** for `accept-fields`.

revisionAdvances.description:
Present on `claim-retained` and `claim-superseded`, and `null` (key
present) on every other kind, including `claim-orphaned` — deliberately not defaulted,
like `retargeted`. Informational only: it changes no `kind`, `decision`,
`availableActions` or commit requirement.

`true` when this is a **tracking** claim, one that stores no revision, and the revision
it renders moves with this pull: after the commit it renders the candidate's line
revision. The entry's kind is still judged on quantity and find number alone. The
move is otherwise visible only by comparing `current.detail.childItemRevisionId` with
`candidate.detail.childItemRevisionId`.

**Never true together with `retargeted`.** `retargeted` is about a *pinned* claim that
upstream moved away from. A pin does not move, so its `revisionAdvances` is `false`.
A tracking claim is never retargeted. A `replace` substitute is `false`. The value is
covered by `diffFingerprint`. A `base` row's advance is reported as
`member-version-advance`.

claimKind.description:
Present on `claim-*` kinds; null elsewhere. Distinguishes a claim created by
**claiming** an upstream edge from one created by **replacing** it. Both dispose
identically; this exists so the UI can explain what is being orphaned.

message.description: Human-readable, already-localized summary. Never parse it — switch on `kind`.

current.description: How the branch renders this member today. **Null for `member-added`.**

candidate.description: How it would render after the pull. **Null for `member-removed`**, and for a `claim-orphaned` resolved by `remove`.

MemberTarget.description: Identifies what the entry is about, independent of before/after state.

edgeId.description: The `Assembly_CI__c` for this member. Null for `base` content, which has no branch-owned record until something claims it.

edgeKey.description:
The **display** key — the eBOM `Assembly__c` line id, or the synthetic key of
branch-local content (see `TreeRow.edgeKey`).
**Not** what a pull correlates on: it moves when a parent item revs, which is exactly why
the diff cannot join on it.

label.description:
Short display label for the member — the **child item's** item number
(`Item__c.Name`). On a `source` target it is the root item's number instead, because
that entry is about the root item and has no child.

rowKey.description:
The `rowKey` of the row this entry is about: in the branch's **current**
tree on a pull preview, in the **left** side's tree on a comparison. A client uses it
to show the entry in the tree. Null when that tree has no such row (`member-added`) and
on a root entry. When the member renders at more than one occurrence, the first in tree
order.

path.description: Breadcrumb from the root to this member's parent, for UI context.

PathSegment.description: One ancestor in a breadcrumb. Same shape as `MemberTarget` minus the path — a segment never nests its own breadcrumb.

MemberState.description: A member as resolved at one point in the diff (before or after). The generic fields are framework-level; everything type-specific lives in `detail`.

AssemblyEdgeDetail.description:
**The one Site BOM-specific schema.** Everything above this point is reusable framework
vocabulary; this is the single place assembly/BOM concepts appear. A second
configuration-item type becomes a sibling schema in `MemberState.detail`'s `oneOf` and
changes nothing else.

## Display fields

`parentItemNumber`, `childItemNumber`, `childItemName` and `childRevisionLabel` are
populated on every read. They are looked
up once per page, never once per row. They are display values: null where the record is
not visible to the caller, so never treat a null as evidence that an item has no number.

parentItemId.description:
The owning **item**, not its revision: an edge's parent item is stable across revision
advances, while its parent revision is not.

**Null on a root entry** — see `quantity` for why.

parentItemNumber.description: The parent item's number (`Item__c.Name`). See the schema description.

childItemNumber.description: The child item's number (`Item__c.Name`). See the schema description.

childItemName.description: The child item's description, for display. See the schema description.

childItemRevisionId.description:
The child revision this row renders. Which clock chose it depends on the row, and the
enclosing `governingTimestamp` does not always name that clock:

- a `base` row resolves at the source's T_R, and `governingTimestamp` is T_R;
- a **tracking** claim (no stored revision) also resolves at T_R — it renders the source
  line's revision — but its `governingTimestamp` is `asOf`, because that one field also
  governs the claim's quantity and find number;
- a **pinned** row (a stored `childItemRevisionId`) renders the pin whatever
  either clock says; its `governingTimestamp` is `asOf`, which chose nothing;
- a floating `new` row or substitute, and every `nested` row, resolve at `asOf`.

A tombstone over a source line keeps the revision of the line it removed; a tombstone of
a branch-local row carries none. Also null on a floating row whose item has nothing
released at `asOf` — the row still renders.

This is the value to send back as `childItemRevisionId` to pin, or keep, what the tree
shows.

childRevisionLabel.description: The label of `childItemRevisionId`. See the schema description.

quantity.description:
**Null on a root entry.** The `source-version-advance` / `root-version-differs` entry at
the top of a pull diff or comparison is about the root *item*, which has no parent, no
quantity and no find number — its `target.ciKind` is `source`, not `assembly-edge`. Every
edge entry populates all three.

findNumber.description: A Salesforce `Number` field, never a string. **Null on a root entry** — see `quantity`.

candidateRootRevisionId.description: The released root revision being accepted. Same validation as the preview's query param — and re-validated here, from the re-resolved diff.

diffFingerprint.description: Echoed back from the preview this commit is acting on. A mismatch against the freshly re-resolved diff fails the whole commit with `STALE_REVISION`.

previewId.description:
The `previewId` of the preview this commit is acting on. Optional in this
version, and checked like `diffFingerprint` when sent: a preview that no longer
describes the diff fails the commit with `STALE_REVISION`. Send it now; a later version
that keeps large diffs server-side will look them up by it.

decisions.description:
One entry per `claim-orphaned` entry from the preview. **Every one must appear**, or
the commit is rejected with `DISPOSITION_REQUIRED`. Send `[]` (or omit) when the preview
had no required entries.

It may also carry **optional** decisions: `accept-fields` (with
`acceptedFields`) on `claim-retained` / `member-add-collision`, and `release` on
`claim-superseded`. An entry left undecided keeps the branch's value.
`DISPOSITION_REQUIRED` keys on `claim-orphaned` alone. A decision whose `action` its
entry does not offer in `availableActions` is `400 INVALID_REQUEST`.

There is **no fixed limit**: send every decision in one commit. A commit too
large for one transaction is refused whole with `413 STRUCTURE_TOO_LARGE`.

entryId.description: An `entryId` from the preview this commit is acting on.

childItemRevisionId.description:
`convert-to-native` only: the child revision to **stamp** onto the
converted row. Same meaning and validation as `DeltaOperation.childItemRevisionId`
on a `convert-to-native` operation, which this is copied onto. "Keep what it
shows" is the orphaned entry's own `current.detail.childItemRevisionId`, sent
back. **Refused** beside any other action — `400 INVALID_REQUEST`
(`childItemRevisionId and trackChildRevision are only taken with
convert-to-native, not with <action>`).

trackChildRevision.description:
`convert-to-native` only: `true` stores no revision, so the converted
row floats at the read clock like an `add`. A `convert-to-native` decision carries
**exactly one** of this and `childItemRevisionId`, or the commit answers
`422 REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` before any delta or acceptance is written.

`true` beside any other action is refused `400 INVALID_REQUEST`;
`false` or absent chooses nothing and is accepted beside
every action, so a client that serialises boolean defaults keeps working.

acceptedFields.description:
`accept-fields` only, and required there; refused beside any other
action. Each key is a field of the entry and each value says what to do with it.
**Name only what you are taking.** An omitted field keeps the branch's own value.
Keys and values are matched **case-insensitively** and echoed in the canonical
form shown here; a key named twice in different case is refused.

| Value | Meaning | Stores |
|---|---|---|
| `candidate` | Hold what upstream resolves now | the candidate's value. For the revision this is a **pin**, which reports `retargeted: true` again when upstream next moves the line. |
| `release` | Stop holding the branch's own value | nothing. For the revision this is the state `trackChildRevision: true` leaves. A claim becomes a tracking claim that follows T_R and still gets a `claim-*` entry on every pull. A native row (`member-add-collision`) floats at the read clock. |

`candidate` and `release` render identically on this pull and differently on
later ones.

Refused with `400 INVALID_REQUEST` (full texts on the commit's 400 response):

- any key other than the three below, including `childItem` and
  `childItemRevision`
- a null or empty object
- a value other than `candidate` / `release`
- a field that does not **actually diverge**, meaning the value the branch holds
  does not differ from the candidate's. A tracking claim holds no revision, so
  its revision never diverges, even when `current` and `candidate` render
  different revisions.
- `candidate` on a field the candidate line leaves blank, or a candidate quantity
  of 0 or less
- `release` on a revision the branch does not hold (a floating collision)
- `release` on `quantity` or `findNumber`, which have no source value to fall
  back to on their own. Use `revert`, or `release` on `claim-superseded`.
- `acceptedFields` on any action other than `accept-fields`

status.description:
`completed` — the pull is committed and every field below is filled in. Always
`completed` in this version. `accepted` (with HTTP 202 and a `jobId`) is reserved for a
background commit.

jobId.description: Reserved; always null in this version.

newSourceRevisionId.description: The `Branch_Source_Rev__c` this commit created — an **insert**, never an update.

acceptedAt.description: When the acceptance was committed, reported to the whole second, as a later read of the same record returns it.

applied.description:
Every entry that took an explicit decision (including a decided
`member-add-collision`), plus every `claim-retained`,
`claim-superseded` and `member-add-converged` outcome — the set a caller needs to
reconcile its held preview against what actually happened. (Re-previewing immediately
after a commit is always `hasChanges: false`, so this is the only place to learn it.)

`member-add-converged` reports `action: "retired"`; see the endpoint description.

AppliedEntry.description:
One outcome the commit is reporting back. Five kinds appear here and no others:
`claim-orphaned` (the decision you supplied), `claim-retained` and `claim-superseded`
(always, decided or not), `member-add-converged` (retired by the commit), and
`member-add-collision` — **only when a decision was taken on it**.

A re-preview straight after a commit is always `hasChanges: false`, so this array is the
only place the retained and superseded outcomes can be read.

kind.description: `member-add-collision` appears only when an `accept-fields` decision was taken on it; an undecided collision is not echoed.

action.description:
What was done, in the decision's **canonical** lowercase spelling (`remove`, not
`Remove`, whatever the request's casing):

- `convert-to-native` or `remove` — the decision supplied for a `claim-orphaned`
  entry.
- `accept-fields` — on a `claim-retained` or `member-add-collision` entry that took
  that optional decision; see `acceptedFields`.
- `release` — on a `claim-superseded` entry that took that optional decision; the
  claim was reverted.
- `retired` — on `member-add-converged`. The commit appended a revert, dropping
  the branch's now-redundant local assertion. No decision is accepted for this kind.
- `null` — on an undecided `claim-retained` or `claim-superseded`, where nothing was
  written.

acceptedFields.description:
The `accept-fields` decision's map in canonical form — field names
`quantity` / `findNumber` / `childItemRevisionId`, values `candidate` / `release`,
whatever the request's casing. `null` for every other action and for undecided entries.

edgeId.description: The branch-owned `Assembly_CI__c` this entry's target names, if any. For a live `replace` substitute's `claim-retained`, the substitute's edge.

CompareSideKind.description:
Which resolution produced a side of a comparison. The right-hand side may be any of the
four; the **left** may only be `branch` or `baseline`, because those are the two objects a
comparison path is rooted at.

Sent as `rightKind` — where it is matched case-insensitively — and returned as
`left.kind` / `right.kind`, always in this lower-case spelling.

CompareKind.description:
What a comparison entry reports. The counterpart to `EntryKind`, which is the **pull's**
vocabulary, and deliberately a separate set: a pull is asymmetric and its kinds name what a
pull would *do*, while a comparison is symmetric and does nothing. `member-added` and
`member-removed` are the two wire values the two vocabularies share, and they mean the same
thing in both.

See the endpoint description for what each one means and when it is emitted.

Comparison.description:
The whole answer to "how do these two configurations differ": what each side was, one entry
per differing correlation key, counts over the complete set, and each side's own warnings.

No envelope, nulls not suppressed, and every collection always `[]` rather than absent —
the same conventions as the rest of this API.

left.description: The side the path named — a branch or a baseline.

identical.description:
True when the two configurations contain the same members with the same content.

Computed over the **whole** comparison, and the same on every page: true exactly when
the comparison has no entry of any kind other than `member-unchanged`. So it reads the
same whether or not the unchanged rows were asked for, and a `root-version-differs`
entry is enough on its own to make it false.

entries.description:
One page of entries: one per differing correlation key — plus every matching one when
`includeUnchanged=true` — ordered by breadcrumb path, then find number, then child item
id, then kind. Always present; empty rather than absent, and empty is the ordinary
shape of an identical comparison.

leftWarnings.description:
Warnings about the **left** side's own resolution — typically `MIXED_REVISION` — plus
`COMPARE_ROOTS_DIFFER`, which is about the pair and is reported here, first, because it
reframes everything below it.

A branch or baseline side carries its resolution's complete warning set, including
`STORED_REVISION_RETIRED`; a baseline side adds its drift canaries,
including `BASELINE_PIN_DRIFT`. A source or `ebom` side stores no revisions
and carries neither.

rightWarnings.description: Warnings about the **right** side's own resolution, populated as `leftWarnings` is (without `COMPARE_ROOTS_DIFFER`). Always present; empty rather than absent.

generatedAt.description:
Server clock at computation time, read **once** for the whole call so the two sides are
never resolved microseconds apart. Not a resolution input — each side publishes its own
clocks.

ComparisonSide.description:
One of the two configurations that were compared: what it was, how it resolved, and on
which clock.

Published for **both** sides rather than echoed only for the one the path named, because a
comparison's answer is unreadable without knowing what was compared — `member-added` means
nothing until the reader knows the right side is a baseline from March rather than the
branch's own source.

id.description: The record this side was addressed by — a `Branch__c`, `Baseline__c`, `Branch_Source__c` or `Item_Revision__c`.

label.description:
The side's own display name where the addressed record has one — `Branch__c.Label__c`
for a branch, `Baseline__c.Name` for a baseline — and the **root item number** otherwise,
so a UI always has something to render beside the column. A `source` and an `ebom` side
are named by what they supply rather than by a record a user would recognise.

rootRevisionId.description: The root `Item_Revision__c` this side resolved to. **Null** when a source has nothing accepted yet.

asOf.description:
The read clock this side was resolved at — the caller's `asOf` / `rightAsOf`, the
server clock when none was supplied, an eBOM revision's release date, or a baseline's
own `resolutionTimePoint`. A baseline echoes the timepoint its **cut** recorded,
which makes it obvious the caller could not have chosen it.

sourceTimePoint.description:
**T_R** — the timepoint this side's `base` content resolves at. Separate from
`asOf` because that is the whole model: a side reporting one number could not explain
its own rows.

An `ebom` side publishes the same value in both, honestly rather than leaving this null:
a raw walk has no acceptance pinning it and no branch content floating above it, so its
traversal clock **is** its T_R. Null only where a source has accepted nothing.

CompareEntry.description:
One difference between the two configurations, keyed by correlation key.

**Not the pull's `DiffEntry`.** That contract names its two states `current` and
`candidate`, which is a lie on a symmetric pair — a baseline compared against a raw eBOM has
no "current" side — and it carries four fields a comparison has no use for. The **leaf**
types are shared deliberately: `MemberTarget`, `MemberState`, `PathSegment` and
`AssemblyEdgeDetail` describe where a member sits and how one side renders it, which is
identical work in both features. Only the envelope differs.

entryId.description:
Stable, opaque handle: a deterministic hash of the kind plus the correlation key,
truncated to 16 hex characters. Never a database id, never positional, never generated —
so a repeated comparison returns the same handles. There is nothing to pass it back to;
it exists so a client can key a row. Do not parse it.

**One entry per correlation key, always** — two entries on one key would collide, which
is why `member-differs` carries `differingFields` rather than splitting into one kind
per field.

differingFields.description:
Which of the three assertable values disagree, in a fixed order so two calls produce
byte-identical lists. Populated on `member-differs`; **empty on every other kind** —
empty rather than null, so a client can iterate unconditionally.

Provenance is deliberately not among them: each side's state already publishes it, and
a provenance-only difference is not a content difference.

message.description: Human-readable, from a Custom Label, with the member's own item number appended. Translated; switch on `kind`, never on text.

left.description: How the **left** side renders this member. **Null on `member-added`.**

right.description: How the **right** side renders this member. **Null on `member-removed`.**

CompareSummary.description:
Counts over the **whole** comparison, on every page — never over one page of entries.

Read the two groups differently. `total` and `byKind` count entries **emitted**, so both
move with `includeUnchanged`. `added`, `removed`, `differing` and `unchanged` count
correlation keys and do not.

total.description: Entries produced — `root-version-differs` and any `member-unchanged` included. Moves with `includeUnchanged`.

added.description: Correlation keys present on the **right** side only.

removed.description: Correlation keys present on the **left** side only.

differing.description: Correlation keys present on both sides whose content disagrees.

unchanged.description:
Correlation keys present on both sides and identical.

**Populated whether or not `includeUnchanged` was set**, which is the point of it: the
default comparison emits no row for an identical member, and a caller still needs to
know how much of the configuration matched without paying for the rows. It therefore
does **not** always equal `byKind['member-unchanged']`, which counts emitted entries and
is `0` by default.

byKind.description:
Count per `CompareKind`, keyed by its wire value, over emitted entries.

**Pre-seeded with all five kinds at zero**, unlike the pull's `DiffSummary`, which
carries only the kinds it observed: a comparison is read by a client rendering a fixed
set of counters, and an absent key would make each one a null check.

RestError.description:
The Site BOM's error shape. Keyed **`code`**, not the framework's `errorCode`.

A 403 body carries the label **only**: naming the object a caller was just denied would hand
them the schema they have no access to. It goes to the debug log instead. A 500 carries
the error type only — enough to tell which class of fault occurred — and never its message
or the stack trace; the full detail goes to the debug log.

code.description:
The stable error code. Every value below is a client error; a 500 carries
`INTERNAL_ERROR`, which is listed here for completeness but is not a code to branch on.

message.description:
The Custom Label for `code`, with a parenthesised **detail** appended naming the specific
row or value. The label says what went wrong and what to do about it; the detail says
which row it happened to. Translated — never parse it.

failures.description:
Present **only** on an atomic delta batch that failed validation. Carries the complete
per-operation failure list, so a caller does not have to find their faults one round trip
at a time.

Forbidden.description:
`FORBIDDEN` (403). The caller lacks an object grant this endpoint requires. The body names no
object — see `RestError`.

A field-level denial is also answered 403: every read on this path uses a fixed set of
fields, so when a query fails, missing field access is far and away the likeliest cause.
The one exception is a query too long for the platform to accept, which only a very large structure produces:
that is `413 STRUCTURE_TOO_LARGE`, not 403.

value.message: You do not have permission to perform this action.

NotFoundPath.description:
`NOT_FOUND` (404). The path id is absent, unparseable, or names a **different object** than
this endpoint expects — the last of which is why swapping a `branchId` for a `sourceId` is a
clean 404 rather than a 500.

Also answered for any unrecognised trailing segment: `GET .../branches/{id}/bogus` is the
Site BOM's own 404 in the Site BOM's own shape (`code`), not the framework's (`errorCode`).

StructureTooLarge.description:
`STRUCTURE_TOO_LARGE` (413). The structure this request has to resolve is too
large to process in one transaction. **Nothing is written.** Sending the same request again
will fail the same way, so do not retry it.

The server checks the platform limits it has actually consumed (CPU time, memory, rows read,
queries, rows written) as it resolves, and stops with this answer before it would run out,
rather than failing with an unhandled error or returning a partial structure. It never
returns part of a structure as if it were the whole.

A smaller page does not help: the limit is about the configuration, not the response.
Depth counts as well as size: pull preview and commit support structures up to 15 levels
deep, and a deeper structure may answer `413 STRUCTURE_TOO_LARGE`. Contact your
administrator. A configuration this large is a candidate for splitting into smaller Site BOMs.
