PullUnprocessable.description:
422 — well formed, but impossible against the model. Retrying the identical request against
the same state will never succeed.

| code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `CANDIDATE_ROOT_MISMATCH` | the candidate belongs to a **different root item** than the source |
| `CYCLE_DETECTED` / `EBOM_CYCLE` | a cycle in the eBOM below the candidate root |
| `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` | the correlation join cannot tell which upstream line corresponds to which branch line — one of the three shapes below |
| `REVISION_CHOICE_REQUIRED` | *commit only* — a `convert-to-native` decision carried neither or both of `childItemRevisionId` and `trackChildRevision: true` |
| `REVISION_ITEM_MISMATCH` | *commit only* — a `convert-to-native` decision's `childItemRevisionId` is not a revision of the row's child item |

`AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` is raised in three shapes. Which remedy applies depends on the
shape, and the message's detail names the edges involved:

1. **A genuine duplicate line.** Two edges on the **same side** share a correlation key
   **and** a parent revision. This is data: the BOM has to change, by giving one of the
   lines its own secondary unique key — unless the pair is two of the branch's own rows
   at one key, which a branch edit clears.
2. **A pairing that would be a guess.** Edges at one key are left on **both** sides under
   different parent revisions, with more than one on a side. Usually data; a branch row in
   the mix can be removed to clear it.
3. **Two unpaired entries at one position.** Two or more edges at one key would be left
   without a counterpart on **one** side as the **same kind** of entry, so under one
   `entryId`, where the diff could report only one of them. Rows that produce no entry
   (`nested` rows, tombstones, branch-native rows) do not count, and neither do two rows
   of different kinds. A `replace` substitute beside a **claimed** line of its new child
   that upstream drops completes while upstream keeps the substitute's superseded line —
   the substitute is `claim-retained` and the claimed line the one `claim-orphaned`.
   Only when upstream drops **both** lines are both
   `claim-orphaned`, and the pull refuses. A branch edit clears it: exclude the
   substitute, or revert the claim on the dropped line, which then reads as
   `member-removed`.

One parent item rendering at two revisions is **not** one of these: the parent revision
separates those lines.

ComparisonUnprocessable.description:
422 — well formed, but impossible against the model. Retrying the identical request against
the same state will never succeed.

| code | Cause |
|---|---|
| `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION` | the correlation join cannot tell which member on one side corresponds to which on the other. The same three shapes as on the pull (see `PullUnprocessable`): two edges on one side sharing a key **and** a parent revision, edges at one key left on both sides under different parent revisions with more than one on a side, or two or more edges at one key left unpaired on one side. A comparison reports every one-sided member on a side as one kind, so for the third shape any two members count — a substitute beside a line of the same child that the other side lacks refuses whether that line is claimed or not — and excluding the substitute clears it, since tombstones are not members. A fourth shape is the comparison's alone: two entries it would publish carry one `entryId` — two pairs at one key reported as the same kind, both `member-differs` or (with `includeUnchanged=true`) both `member-unchanged`. That happens when both configurations hold a substitute beside a line of the same child, or a claimed line beside a local `add` of the same child, and either both rows changed (two `member-differs`) or neither did and `includeUnchanged=true` (two `member-unchanged`). With one row changed, or with neither changed and `includeUnchanged` off, the comparison completes. Removing or reverting one of the branch's changes at that position clears it. Known gap: when the two sides' root items differ (`COMPARE_ROOTS_DIFFER`) the comparison runs no join and this check does not apply, so two members at one key on one side — such a substitute and its line, say — are published as two `member-removed` (or `member-added`) entries under one `entryId` rather than refused. On a baseline side no branch edit clears any of these: a baseline cannot be edited. One parent item rendering at two revisions is not one of them |
| `CYCLE_DETECTED` | a cycle in the eBOM beneath either side's root, so that side cannot be resolved at all |

Both sides are resolved, so either can raise either code. `AMBIGUOUS_CORRELATION`'s detail
names the offending side in the **comparison's** own vocabulary — `left side`,
`right side`, or `right and left sides` — where a pull's says `current` and `candidate`.
The label before it is shared with pull-preview; switch on `code`, and read the ids rather
than the nouns.

A comparison always reports a cycle as **`CYCLE_DETECTED`**, never as the traversal's own
`EBOM_CYCLE`: the two mean the same thing to a caller and are both 422, and carrying the
inner code out would make this contract depend on which internal walk happened to find it.
A tree read, which has one walk and no such choice, still answers `EBOM_CYCLE`.

If two BOM lines are genuine duplicates, give one its own secondary unique key. If this branch's own changes are among them, such as a substitute beside another line of the same part, exclude the substitute first, or in a pull revert your claim on that other line; otherwise remove or revert one of your changes at that position. A baseline cannot be edited, so these remedies apply only to the live branch.
